content.text: In the new era, however, the technologies developed by the leading engineers, biologists and computer scientists have been developed to make the successful construction of autonomous running machines look realistic. This book contains the results of the DFG's priority program "Autonomous Running" - which is based on an intensive collaboration between leading engineers, biologists and computer scientists in this field. It presents the successes of the technical realization of running machines, as well as the latest biological findings, which directly incorporate their results into such technical implementations. These include questions of topological structures of running, the problem of control and control and related questions of sensors and actuators, the modelling of dynamics and the design and construction of selected running machines. content.text: Lexical-functional grammar: an introduction to the example of French with computer linguistic implementation. Among the various grammar models that today represent the state of research, lexical-functional grammar is one of those that can be implemented on the computer and thus enable an incorruptible review of grammatical analyses. Using this preference, this introduction combines grammatical description and analysis with its implementation. It introduces step by step into the model and simultaneously develops a grammar for a section of French. For the implementation, XLE is used, a widely proven software. The book also shows how flexion morphology can be implemented as finite state morphology and integrated into the syntax fragment. As far as French grammar is concerned, the following topics are dealt with, among other things: congruence, the clitic subject pronouns, the adjective, the prepositions, the determinence, the sentence-like complements, the infinitive constructions and the control verbs, the passive, the auxiliar selection of the tempus periphrases, and a particular section of the computer's and the mathematical language processing.
content.title_en: Lexical-functional grammar : an introduction to the example of French with computer linguistic implementation

content.text: The Moses puzzle: on the trail of a biblical invention. The question of the historicity of the Bible is as little new as that of the historicality of Moses. It is therefore legitimate when an Egyptologist of the Humboldt University in Berlin questions the historicity of Moses, the Pentateuch and some prophets for a non-academic audience, calls it an invention and opens up an Egyptian prince behind the legend of Moses. Less legitimate is that a book based on science, which argues with research results, contains no evidence for his theses despite its special titles of comprehensive bibliography. However, historicality does not matter, according to Heidelberg Egyptologist J. Assmann ("Moses of the Egyptians", ID 26/98), but rather the "Mosaic distinction" between true and untrue in religion, memory culture and tradition of thinking about God and the origin of monotheism: the title is called, but reference is not taken to it. However, it cannot do much harm. (3) (Friedrich Andrae)
content.title_en: The Moses puzzle : in the footsteps of a biblical invention

content.text: Survey interviews : Methods of standardized surveys. This textbook provides detailed information on the conduct of standardized surveys, especially of the general population. The book deals with general problems of question formulation and response behaviour. Special attention is paid to practical problems of questionnaire design and the execution of pretests. For all forms of standardized interviews (written, oral, telephone, via internet) the particularities of the survey instruments, the sampling procedure and the implementation are presented in practice. Here, above all non-response problems are discussed in detail and possibilities for their avoidance are presented.
content.title_en: Survey interviews : Methods of standardized surveys

content.text: The history of climate change: from the Ice Age to global warming. After a brief introduction to the development of climate in Earth's history to the appearance of man, historian Behringer describes in the main the influence of climate change on the rise and decline of civilizations around the world. One focus is the medieval climate optimum and the small ice age in the 16th and 17th centuries as well as the present anthropogenic influenced global warming. He shows that already small climate changes had great effects on the everyday life of people, on fashion, architecture, culture, religion, economy, politics and society order. Earlier ways out of the crisis were e.g. the neolithic and the industrial revolution. The author therefore calls for a more rational handling of climate change and an adaptation to the changing conditions. Other focal points than "climate change" (ID 37/07). This readable and thoughtful book is an important complement to "a short natural history of the last millennium change" by J. Reichholf (BA 6/07) and "a short history of climate change" by K. Ludwig (BA 12/06).
content.title_en: Cultural history of the climate : from the ice age to global warming

content.text: Cultural tourism for everyone? : new strategies for a growth market. Cultural tourism is changing. With offers off the classic cultural business, organizers try to respond to changing needs of travellers. But does it actually succeed in reaching people beyond the traditional cultural audience? And is there finally even the prospect of a transfer back to the cultural business? This volume takes into consideration hitherto neglected manifestations of cultural tourism in the discussion, which elude a typical classification by means of divisions and institutions. An illuminating contribution to the debate on the challenges of cultural tourism. (Verlagstext)
content.title_en: Cultural tourism for all? : new strategies for a growth market

The bicycle is affordable for everyone, as evidenced by its spread in India or China today or in Europe and North America in the 19th century. content.text: The conquest of Mexico: Cortés and Montezuma. This is the first great representation of the conquest of Mexico for over 150 years. Hugh Thomas designs an impressive and colourful painting of the encounter between two cultures, thinking and mentality. He resurrects the old Aztec empire with its capital Tenochtitsln and describes in an exciting way the military actions that sealed the demise of the world empire. Above all, however, he portrays the acting persons with the proven, clear view of the fishing for characters and their peculiarities - above all the two protagonists Cortés and Montezuma.

A CD, which includes the system and an interactive preparation of the text, is included. However, the author is not limited to specifying computational rules with programming instructions, but represents the selected topics rounded and mathematically complete. The beginning is simple divisibility properties. Extensive discussion of chain breaks and their applications is detailed. A very nice section on cryptology is a shorter one. The comprehensiblely formulated book hardly requires more than school knowledge. (2 S) (Wolfgang Grölz)

content.text: The amateur researcher Rauter presents a history of 20th century civil underwater shipping. He begins with the German submarines in World War I (about 1/3 of the size), deals with offshore marine technology, deep-sea research and tourist submarines. Broader space takes up Piccard's and Cousteau's services. The work represents a successful mixture of material objectivity, a generally understandable text, and an appealing illustration. It should be before the thematically closer N. Gierschner: Diving boats (BA 1/81, 409). (2) (Martin Paulini) Picture-text-book on the history of 20th century civil underwater shipping. content.text: Walter Gropius, the Bauhaus in Dessau : from the idea to the form. The Kursorische Geschichte des Bauhaus, in which the famous university of the same name was based, ranges from planning to the present day and encompasses a wide range of uses. Since the building cannot be seen in isolation from the ideas of its creators and the ones who work in it, the basic principles of the Bauhaus school are also evident. The urban architect and architectural historian understands how to write scientifically correct, concisely and yet understandable. Well equipped with floor plans, time table, overview of the teachers and bibliography there. Not comparable with the much more profoundly "The Bauhaus Building in Dessau" (ID 10/99). (2) (Martin Paulini)
content.title_en: Walter Gropius, the Bauhaus in Dessau : from the idea to the form

content.text: The socialization of nature: studies on the social evolution of practical reason. With "nature" the social sciences have never been able to do much. One left the reflection on nature to the natural sciences and their appropriation to the technical disciplines. However, it becomes increasingly clear that this division of labour between nature and social sciences does not meet the ecological conditions. Only the view on the symbolic appropriation of nature, on the communication that enables it and through it is made possible makes the social nature relationship visible. This thesis is unfolded – in the use of symbolic anthropology and political economy – on phenomena such as essenabus and fast food, cannibalism and vegetarianism, romantic and industrial nature relations, natural food movement and industrial exploitation of nature.
content.title_en: The socialization of nature : studies on the social evolution of practical reason

content.text: The Infinite: mathematicians struggle for a term. Pythagoras and the Infinite in the Pentagram -- Euclid and the Infiniteness of Prim Numbers -- Archimedes and the Infinite Exhaustion -- Newton and the Infinite in the Movement -- Cantor and the Infinite Decimal Numbers -- Hilbert and the Infinite Certainty -- Brouwer and the Infinite Freedom Philosophers and theologians have thought about the Infinite. But the true science of the Infinite is mathematics. Rudolf Taschner manages to convey this central concept to the mathematical layman. In a vivid way, he describes how Pythagoras, Archimedes and Euclid have already tried to grasp the Infinite. He makes us acquainted with Newton and Leibniz, who discovered that the phenomenon of movement and change is only understood by the study of the Infinite. Can their conclusions be understood or controlled? In the political context, the question arises who owns the algorithms and data, the means of production of the AI economy, who controls them and who bears responsibility for their decisions. If artificial intelligence influences credit contracts, job allocation, the amount of insurance contributions and even jurisdiction, if language assistants constantly accompany our everyday lives, what does that mean for the individual? While neurosciences are making great progress in the undertaking to demonstrate the effect of brands, it is important for economists to quantify these effects. This is mainly due to the fact that different people react to stimuli in different ways. If consumers show heterogeneous needs and behavioural forms, it is useful to combine these to homogeneous segments and to work differently. However, empirical measurements often cause the problem that the sources of heterogeneity are not known or tangible. Lars Köster develops a model for measuring brand strength in the presence of such latent structures. content.text: Performance measurement of stochastic service productions. Services are intangible goods whose creation requires the integration of an external factor. For the service producer, this external factor is often an uncertainty factor, since its quality is determined by the customer. Marcel Rossmy examines how stochastic service productions can be assessed. On production and efficiency theory bases, he analyses known performance measurement methods for their suitability for the evaluation of stochastic productions. The author develops a two-stage methodology based on data development analysis and expectation-benefit theory. To analyse the overall efficiency of a company, new indicators are introduced for the evaluation of production, adaptation and selection efficiency. Using the example of rehabilitation measures, he illustrates the application of the presented methodology and discusses extension possibilities and generalizations. Thus, the proposed methodology can be considered in particular as a basis for a stochastic production theory. Taking into account the uncertainty in service productions to be assessed, he describes the application of the presented methodology and discusses the generalizations. Thus, the proposed methodology can be considered in particular as a basis for a stochastic production theory.
content.title_en: Performance measurement of stochastic service productions

content.text: The European Retirement Facility (Mtgage Covered Bonds) and the Mortgage Backed Securities (Mtgage) in Europe. The mortgage loan business is very important throughout Europe. However, when refinancing the loans with deposits and unsecured bonds, the advantage of using the financed real estate and the loans granted for it as security and thus to reduce the cost of the loan is not used. This guarantee is the essential characteristic of Mortgage Covered Bonds and Mortgage Backed Securities, which are now used for refinancing in various European countries. In this context, the book is aimed at investigating mortgage loan transactions on major European markets, analysing the use of Mortgage Covered Bonds and Mortgage Backed Securities and their costs. In addition, it is shown how the use of the instruments and the legal framework can be improved in the field of business management at the University of Duisburg.
content.title_en: Covered instruments for refinancing mortgage loans: An analysis of Mortgage Covered Bonds and Mortgage Backed Securities in European Countries

content.text: Measurement technology : System theory for electrical engineers. This textbook deals with the system technical and system theoretical principles of measurement technology. The common methods common to all measurement systems are highlighted, which describe the physical behaviour by a mathematical model, improve the static and dynamic properties of measuring systems, measure stochastic quantities and collect data in the digital computer.For a better connection to the theory of stochastic processes, the theoretical foundations and the systematic classification of signal classes are summarized.The term power density is introduced and the Viennese filter is presented. Further topics are a comprehensive system theoretical description of errors in digital measurement data acquisition as well as the recording of frequency analogue signals. The 7th edition has been corrected and updated.
content.title_en: Measurement technology : System theory for electrical engineers

content.text: The relevance of the fair value assessment of investment properties was assessed in the context of IFRS: A deductive and empirical study of the pre-preferential value of alternative heuristics with regard to relevance and reliability. Problem assessment -- Thematic classification and demarcation -- Course of investigation -- Conceptual framework and methodological preliminary considerations -- Illustration of investment properties according to IAS 40 -- Problem clarification and definition -- Problem solving framework for the mapping of investment properties to fair value -- Inductive and deductive considerations for problem solving -- Empirical investigation -- Classification and objective -- Method selection and theoretical principles -- Data evaluation -- Interpretation and implications. The International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) accounting is mostly used to provide decision-making information. IAS 40 collects the claim to provide such information and therefore calls for fair value analysis of investment properties. Fair value is generally used to estimate the lack of current comparison prices in Germany with the help of a DCF procedure, but does not include specific guidelines on this. Christian Huschke uses an empirical analysis of the alternative problem-solving approach.
content.title_en: Real estate valuation in the context of IFRS : A deductive and empirical investigation of the pre-eminence of alternative heuristics regarding relevance and reliability in the fair value assessment of investment properties

content.text: Women, politics and media. content.text: Motor vehicles in income and VAT law: From purchase to sale. The authors describe the tax treatment of motor vehicles in practice, from purchase to daily use to sale. Here you look at the facts from both a tax and a VAT perspective. Numerous changes have been made to this legal area through legislation, jurisprudence and financial management. The work now presents the current state of all important questions and provides tax-optimized and practical solutions. The main focus of the work are: - Assignment to the operating assets - 1% method - Travel book method as well as in - Assignment to the business area - Pretax deduction - Vehicle use by the entrepreneur Numerous overviews and examples make the work a valuable means of work and allow quick access to the topic.

content.text: Decisionability of Petri Networks : Overview and Compendium. Petri Networks and their Mathematics -- The Accessibility Problem -- Elementary Marking Problems -- Fire Sequences and Languages -- Petri Networks with Zero Test -- Overview. Petri Networks are the most widely considered and best studied model for parallel invoices and places/transition networks, the most famous and most important class of Petri Networks. In this book, for the first time, all important questions about the decisionability of classical locations/transition networks are systematically compiled and discussed. This includes, for example, the accessibility problem further questions that deal with markings and languages of Petri Networks, such as the accessibility of quantities of markings, the reproduction of markings and various concepts of vitality, or the question whether the language of a Petri network is e.g. empty, finite, total, regular, equal to another language. Various classic language and acceptance models of Petri Networks are considered.

content.text: Supply Performance Measurement : Performance measurement in purchasing and supply management. For several years, research and practice have been discussing the further development of supply management's procurement in the context of declining value-added levels. In order to make the potential of external value-added usable for the company usable, the question of measuring and controlling the performance of supply management is at the center of interest. However, the establishment of such supply performance measurement systems has so far posed significant challenges to research and practice. Based on the methodology of applied management research, Aiko Entchelmeier is developing an integrated performance management approach to establishing performance management.
content.title_en: Supply Performance Measurement : Performance measurement in Purchasing and Supply Management

content.text: Acquisition-related value change of acquisition subjects: A synergy- and acquisition-based model. In connection with the acquisition of companies, acquisition-related value losses of acquisition subjects are often observed. Karsten Klopfer determines the net synergy and the acquisition premium as value-influencing factors. In an empirical study, he shows that the net synergy for the owners of the acquisition subject is limited and over-expanded acquisition premiums are paid, which explain the loss of value of acquisition subjects. He empirically derives a relationship that enables a forecast of the change in value of the acquisition subject from the amount of the acquisition premium granted. Compared to a frequently applied trading strategy, acquisition subjects could be sold empty when the acquisition announcement was made, thanks to the application of the model also to significant performance increases in the future. Basic -- Model for acquisition-related value change of acquisition subjects -- Empirical results of the company's empirical analysis - Application of the empirical results - Application of the acquisition claims to the acquisition entities.
content.title_en: Acquisition-related change in value of acquisition subjects : A synergy- and acquisition-based model

content.text: The contributions of this volume discuss the current shifts in the discourse of capitalism analysis and critique, which respond to the "neoliberal" transformation of the capitalist system. They are guided by the question of how to conceive a theoretically coherent and practically promising critique of capitalism, after the classical instruments of social critique have been discredited in many ways and have proved to be dull and outdated.The first part of the volume gathers contributions in which important strands of current critique of capitalism are presented.
content.title_en: Metamorphoses of capitalism – and its criticism

Thus, you learn from technical examples to develop your memory capacity, read technical texts faster and how to keep your oral lecture completely free. content.text: Optimization of cooperative services in engineering customer service. The design and optimization of technical customer services, which are provided cooperatively in network structures, is becoming more important for many companies. The measurement, evaluation and feedback of performance-critical information required for this purpose, taking into account the requirements of different cooperation partners, plays a crucial role in the company's success. Tanja Klostermann shows in the technical customer service of mechanical engineering that technical services provided in network structures can be continuously optimized and controlled by the application of a control system, similar to technical processes. She examines the measurement, evaluation, control and optimization of cooperatively performed performance processes. On this basis, the author presents a solution concept for the development of a control system for the optimization of service processes and provides recommendations for their cooperation-based design. content.text: Street as a cultural space for action: Interdisciplinary considerations of the street space at the interface between theory and practice. The street, probably the most heterogeneous and active space in our society, is a space of the public, which can be entered by every citizen, influenced and thus co-designed. In order to be able to illustrate this spatial variety of action and effects textually, all contributions in this volume take a different focus into consideration. At the interface of scientific theory and project-oriented practice, the connection between ethnographic, sociological, artistic, media, economic, political, architectural, geographical, sport, cultural and communication-scientific views emerges from the so far unical spectrum of approaches to the urban street space, which can show where and by which ways the street can be 'read' and 'described'.
content.title_en: Street as a cultural action space : Interdisciplinary considerations of the street space at the interface between theory and practice

content.text: Concepts of object-oriented programming: With an introduction to Java. Object orientation: An introduction -- objects, classes, encapsulation -- inheritance and subtyping -- Building blocks for object-oriented programs -- object-oriented program frameworks -- parallelity in object-oriented programs -- programming of distributed objects -- summary, variants, outlook. The book provides a compact introduction to the concepts of object-oriented programming. It explains the object and class concept, describes encapsulation techniques and goes into detail on subtyping and inheritance. Software reuse in the form of library modules and program frameworks (frameworks) is discussed using the example of processing streams and the construction of graphical user interfaces. Furthermore, important concepts of parallel and distributed programming are discussed and the practical connection to object orientation is established. Each object-oriented concept is first introduced in general, i.e. independently of a programming language. Afterwards its concrete programming language implementation in Java is explained in detail.

content.text: From the transformation to the openness of cooperation? : The opening of the legal systems of selected countries of Central and Eastern Europe to the law of peoples and Europe. Why and how far have the countries of Central and Eastern Europe opened their respective legal systems to supranational legal systems - international law and Community law - is the main question of work? And is there a constitutionally supported cooperation readiness in the countries studied? The most important feature of this opening is the analysis of the existence, form and limits of the transformation of the rules of supranational legal systems into a complementary legal source. The findings thus gained stem from the thesis that there is a specific relationship between the extent of this opening and the quality of the rule of law of the respective national legal system: the more open a legal system is, the greater the probability that it is also legal state. The book focuses on the question of why and how far the countries of Central and Eastern Europe have opened their legal systems to supranational legal systems such as international law and Community law. The most important feature of the opening is the author's analysis of the form and limits of the transformation of the rules of the law into a legal system is the same as a source of openness.
content.title_en: From transformation to openness to cooperation? : Opening up the legal systems of selected countries in Central and Eastern Europe to international and European law

content.text: Price formation of medicines in international comparison. Pharmaceutical markets are regulated by law in almost all industrial nations. This includes above all pricing, usually across all distribution stages, from the manufacturer, through wholesalers, pharmacies, health insurance companies to patients. The book provides an overview of the different pricing strategies of the comparative countries Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, Netherlands, Spain, Great Britain, Australia, Canada, USA and Japan. In particular, freely available and prescription drugs are used for international comparison, as both types are subject to different price formation influences across the distribution stages. Starting from a theoretical view, market economy, state and other factors of influence as well as their empirical influence on price formation and distribution margins are discussed with the aim of making effective patient prices of medicines internationally comparable. Theory of price formation at the manufacturer level -- Composition of patient price: Further price formation levels -- Price formation of medicines in international comparison: Order policy framework -- International price differentiation in practice -- Discussion of international drug pricing systems -- Summary and outlook.

content.text: The study EduCare provides the first results on the design of the pedagogical quality for children in the different school forms: day school, school with block-time lessons and school with traditional teaching and possible differences. Furthermore, pedagogical quality features of the family are described and differences between the families of the children who attend the different school forms are analysed. The results show that the comparison of day school children with intensive use in terms of the level of development in school performance in language, socio-emotional development as well as the development of everyday skills compared to children who attend the traditional or block-time lessons is in favour of day school children. Marianne Schüpbach is a senior assistant and project manager at the University of Bern, Institute of Education, Department of Educational Psychology.
content.title_en: Full-day education and primary education: quality and effectiveness of different types of school compared

These are companies that develop, manufacture or maintain parts, components, assemblies and engines for aircraft or aircraft themselves. (technical) aviation industry has a significant specificity in contrast to other industries, as their activities are determined by the regulations of the relevant air inspectorates. content.text: Green IT, virtualization and thin clients: Reaching energy efficiency with new IT technologies, protecting the environment and saving costs. Entrepreneurs, IT managers, IT consultants and scientists are confronted with increasing IT performance and security requirements while simultaneously compulsioning them to save energy and costs. Thin clients and virtualization or server based computing offer an ecologically and economically advantageous alternative to traditional PC networks. This book enables a quick introduction to the basics of these technologies and presents the economic and ecological advantages, including based on recent studies by Fraunhofer Institute UMSICHT. Based on practical cases, the achieved savings and environmental benefits are demonstrated.The content: Energy efficiency in the data centerEsstablishment savings through virtualizationDesktop virtualization Thin clients: Introduction, economicity and ecologyNational and European environmental impactGreen Best Practice: Case studies from companies as well as public and private organizationsThe target group:- IT managers, administrators- environmental and cost-conscious entrepreneurs- IT consultants and marketing experts in the IT department.

content.text: The taxation of foreign family foundations according to the Foreign Tax Act: Analysis and Perspectives. Foreign family foundations have been evaluated early on in the consulting practice as a suitable design building block for the wealth succession planning. Due to the progressive internationalization foreign family foundations will increasingly be looking into the field of foreign family foundations in the future. However, German foreign tax law has substantial sanctions available to prevent the establishment of foreign family foundations. Kay Alexander Schulz examines these regulations from a systematic, Community and constitutional perspective and develops guiding principles for a pre-determined redesign of the taxation of foreign family foundations. Introduction -- Fundamentals of the investigation -- The access taxation of § 15 AStG -- Effects of Community law on the access system of foreign family foundations -- Effects of constitutional law on the access system of foreign family foundations -- Approaches for a reformed access control of foreign family foundations -- Summary of the main results.

content.text: Injection pressure of modern passenger car diesel engines: influence on soot emission. Soot emission in diesel-engine combustion -- models of injection-jet-guided mixture formation -- influence of external exhaust gas return on soot emission -- influence of injection pressure on soot emission -- model for the two-phase area within the fuel beam -- validation of the model by motor investigations -- summary. The exhaust gas return is also one of the most important measures of internal motor reduction of NOx emissions in the passenger car diesel engine in the future. The NOx reduction potential is directly coupled with the receipt of low soot values with high back-guided exhaust emissions. Yvan Gauthier investigates how the high kinetic energy of the fuel beam can be implemented in partial load mode in such a way that the soot emission in the exhaust gas is significantly reduced. He first analyses the conventional car diesel combustion method and introduces new parameters in order to establish a correlation between input sizes of the engine with the soot emission in the exhaust gas. In the main part, he develops a two-phase fuel emission of the fuel emission, which is then the fuel emission of the fuel.
content.title_en: Injection pressure with modern passenger car diesel engines : influence on the soot emission

content.text: Statistics : An understandable introduction. This textbook of statistical data analysis was designed specifically for introductory courses and is aimed at all those who are looking for an easy-to-understand introduction to social science statistics. It refers to the field of educational and social sciences and does not treat the material as content-independent mathematical knowledge. They learn: - The basic methods of descriptive and inference statistics - The most important techniques of graphical representation - The logic of statistical argumentation - The basic principles of more complex statistical methods - Outputs of SPSS or SYSTAT to read correctly - Results of statistical analyses to interpret - Results of research projects to understand Dr. Udo Kuckartz is professor of empirical educational science and methods of social research at the Philipps University Marburg, heads the Marburg working group Methods Evaluation (MAGMA) and has many years of experience in statistical education. Stefan Rädker is a research associate at MAGMA and teaches methods of social research and social science data analysis. Thomas Ebert is a research associate, Julia Schehl is a research associate at MAGMA.
content.title_en: Statistics : An understandable introduction

content.text: The demographic impact of urban housing districts: development scenarios and options for action. Dr. Olaf Schnur is a representative professor of human geography at the Institute of Geography of the University of Potsdam. His main areas of work are urban and social geography, urban development in large cities and social urban development. At the urban development-politically so important level of residential districts there were for a long time only few research work with regard to demographic processes. This is no coincidence, because "the district" withdraws simple analyses. Olaf Schnur opens up new content and methodical perspectives: Using an investigation of four German cities he explores demographically and structurally differently structured residential districts in a creative mix of methods (including scenario technology, Delphi method). This will result in development scenarios within the framework of a residential district typology, "tools" for municipalities and the housing industry ("quartiersentwicklungsmanagement") as well as a demographically oriented, cyclical governance model of the district development. Individual types of teaching can be assigned to the district management of the urban district management.
content.title_en: Demographic impact in urban housing: development scenarios and options

content.text: Property-oriented description of the logical architecture of embedded systems. Logical architecture -- Formal foundations -- Basics of property-oriented architecture description -- Illustrative representation of property-oriented architecture specification -- Property-oriented architecture patterns -- Case study -- Summary and outlook. Automotive embedded systems are complex distributed networks consisting of numerous hardware and software subsystems. Many functionalities are distributed and can only be provided by the interaction of several subsystems. The logical architecture design, in which the specification of network architecture and distributed functionalities takes place, is therefore an essential part of the development process. In order to reduce the quality assurance effort and achieve high product quality, a specification of behavior and functionality is already important in the system design, which does not allow for ambiguities and at the same time allows precise definition of free spaces for further system development. David Trachtenherz develops the solution approach of property-oriented description of the logical architecture of embedded systems, which supports a precise declarative specification of functional properties with selectable degree of abstraction for different development phases and levels.
content.title_en: Property-oriented description of the logical architecture of embedded systems

Tailored to meet the need for practical background knowledge, the Auto-Fachmann finds a comprehensive overview of the structure and functioning of today's hybrid vehicles, including fuel cells and alternative fuels, an overview of transmissions and a detailed presentation of the electronic transmission control system. The belt offers the Bosch specialist knowledge first-hand and is therefore ideally suited for the everyday life of the development engineer, for the professional
content.title_en: Conventional powertrain and hybrid drives

content.text: International Contract Logistics: Theory and Practice also for smaller companies. International Contract Logistics as a Challenge for Small and Medium-sized Logistics Companies -- International Contract Logistics -- Implications of International Contract Logistics Process Research -- Internationalization Strategies of Logistics SMEs – Empirical Analysis -- Development of a Guide for the Implementation of International Contract Logistics Projects in SMEs -- Overall Conclusion and Recommendations for Action. In the field of contract logistics, no fundamental scientific analysis has yet been carried out. In this area, there is also a great discrepancy between operational practice and scientific discourse. The book therefore scientifically works on this topic and translates the results into a practice-oriented internationalization guide. Initially, the implications of internationalization process theories for international contract logistics are analysed for SMEs, in order to then present the results of empirical quantitative and qualitative studies on internationalization strategies or success factors of internationalization of logistics SMEs. Finally, these results are translated into a guide that analyses information for successful internationalization in practice using checklists and presents them with clear examples.
content.title_en: Internationalization in contract logistics : Theory and practice for smaller companies

Based on relevant laws, guidelines and standards, a detailed content model for instructions is presented. The author describes in detail the process of documentation creation from project planning to translation and provides an insight into the daily work of the technical editor. Practically designed and illustrated chapters deal with the special requirements for the formulation of guiding texts and their functional and target group-oriented design. The selection and the correct use of visualization options are treated as well as the modular creation of instructions and the specificities of the US market. Table of Contents -- Basic -- Laws, guidelines and standards -- Documentation process -- Formulating instructions -- Design instructions -- Design instructions -- Designing safety instructions -- Visualisation -- Instructions modularly create -- Editorial guidelines -- Instructions for the US market -- The instructions in the business context -- Index.

content.text: Request-generating systems: Application analysis, implementation and optimization concepts. Flexible data access is essential in current information systems to meet the increased user requirements. Generating approaches are therefore used in a wide range of application areas to provide specific instructions for data access. Holger Schwarz discusses approaches to request generation and highlights implementation and optimization concepts. He explains the generation approaches in specific application scenarios from areas such as business intelligence, workflow management and search technologies. The spectrum covered ranges from individual applications to tools used in application development. The second focus is on current approaches to the optimization of complex structures of generated data access. These are presented and their optimization potential are demonstrated in sample scenarios. content.text: Semantic Technologies: Basic Concepts – Applications. This textbook provides a comprehensive introduction to basics, potentials and applications of semantic technologies. These elements allow to describe the knowledge contained in information formally and thus to be processed for the computer, to present concepts and relationships and finally to ask content for, open and accessible in networks. content.text: Line diagrams in knowledge communication : A mathematical-didactical study. Being able to represent and communicate knowledge is an important prerequisite for participation in today's knowledge society. Line diagrams from formal conceptual analysis as part of a conceptual knowledge processing are a good means of enabling and stimulating communication of knowledge. Starting from a philosophical consideration of the meaning of line diagrams in knowledge processing, diagrams are presented as means of communication that bridge the gap between users and mathematical-logical representations, as well as between our everyday thinking and formal representations. Good line diagrams can be characterized in terms of their expressive power and strength to support communication processes in their meaning for knowledge communication. For this purpose, it is identified which thought actions are activated and trained in the creation and subsequent use of line diagrams. Finally, didactical basic assumptions and concrete elaborations of the learning environment for formal conceptual analysis are presented.

content.text: Partitioning for efficient duplicate recognition in relational data. Duplicates or duplicates are several data sets that describe the same real world object, for example multiple customers in a CRM system or different representations of a product. Finding these duplicates is a complex and time-consuming task for modern computers, too. Uwe Draisbach compares two of the relevant partitioning strategies that make an intelligent selection of dataset pairs to compare. From this he develops a generalized procedure and shows that an intelligent selection of dataset pairs can significantly reduce the effort without significantly reducing the quality of duplicate recognition. The work was awarded the "Information Quality Best Master Degree Award" by the German Society for Information and Data Quality. Duplicate recognition -- Blocking methods -- Windowing methods -- Comparison Blocking and Sorted-Neighborhood method -- Generalized method.

content.text: Parameter extraction of semiconductor components: Simulation with PSPICE. Complementary to lecture, to computational exercises and in particular to the laboratory internship in the electronics field, analytical methods for the extraction of SPICE model parameters of selected semiconductor components are presented. For components from the DEMO version of the OrCAD-PSPICE program, it is shown how their static and dynamic electric model parameters can be recovered with SPICE analyses. This parameter determination is presented for switching diodes, capacity diodes, Z diodes, npn bipolar transistors, N-channel spheroidal field effect transistor, CMOS array transistors, operating amplifiers and optocouplers. content.text: Parallel programming. Introduction -- Architecture of parallel platforms -- Parallel programming models -- Performance analysis of parallel programs -- Thread programming -- Message-Passing Programming -- Linear equation systems -- Nonlinear equation systems. Through cost-effective multiprocessor desktop computers, clusters of PCs and innovations such as hyperthreading technology or multicore processors, parallel computing resources are omnipresent. However, the efficient use of this parallel computing power is only possible through the use of parallel programming techniques, which thus spread to all areas of software creation. This book presents parallel programming for conventional parallel computers and for the novel parallel platforms comprehensively. In addition to the basics of parallel programming, portable programming environments such as pthreads, Java threads, OpenMP, MPI, PVM or UPC are presented in detail and the additional programming models are discussed. Parallel programming techniques leading to the successful realization of efficient parallel programs are presented with a variety of examples.
content.title_en: Parallel programming

content.text: Decision-making procedure for complex problems: A heuristic approach. Introduction:- Part I: Decision-making problems and decision-making procedures -- Part II: A general heuristic decision-making process -- Part III: Special problems and approaches to their solution -- Glossary -- Index of relevant words -- Bibliography. The most important task of executives is to make decisions of great importance. This is a difficult task, because the important decisions are usually complex. This book presents a decision-making process with which complex problems can be dealt with gradually. Compared to other texts on decision-making methodology, the statements place great emphasis on problem analysis, variant development and the development of the decision-making matrix. The book is suitable for executives who, however, are well-founded in practice with the management of complex problems. content.text: Democratisation and Decentralization: State Organisational Reforms in the Context of Change of Regime and Government in Spain, Poland and Great Britain. Democratisation -- Transition -- Decentralization -- State Organisational Reform -- Context -- Institutions The transition from authoritarianism to democracy not only led to the introduction of democratic institutions in the political centres in the European states, but also had consequences for the entire state structure. A complex division of tasks and powers between the centre, regional and local levels was accompanied by the political system changes. Political decentralization, which, due to its symbolic and "technical" importance, was one of the institutional priorities of democratization, was subject to the conditions of political system change. Philip Stöver's study examines the interactions between these processes, using the democratisation and decentralisation processes in Spain and Poland. Comparison with the British state organisational reforms, which have taken place in a consolidated democracy, shows that the concrete decentralization processes of Spain and Poland cannot be explained without reference to the democratisation context.
content.title_en: Democratisation and Decentralisation: State Organisational Reforms in the Context of Change of Regime and Government in Spain, Poland and Great Britain

content.text: Theoretical approaches to dealing with periphericization -- Empirical results from German mid-city cities -- Findings of further studies. content.text: Negotiations in consensus procedure: Variants of collective decision-making in expert bodies. Expert bodies aim at negotiating results, which are shared by a wide range of experts and stakeholders. Their decision-making processes follow an informal procedure, in which formal coordination is usually dispensed with and the collective decision is made by the absence of open resistance. This mode of consensus allows power asymmetries between the parties involved to emerge and leads to a variance of actual levels of approval. Eva Krick shows which mechanisms of agreement in the informal consensus procedure work, how actors are excluded and selective consent is achieved, but under which circumstances the interests of all parties is also possible. content.text: The Basics of Digital Information Transmission: From Theory to Mobile Applications. The Basics of Applied Information Theory -- Basics of Channel Encoding -- Digital Modulation and Transmission Procedures -- The Basics of Digital Information Transmission (MIM) is a topic of interest to the Department of Information Technology and Communication Technology. content.text: The influence of children on marital stability: Empirical analysis with data from the family survey. Theories of marital instability and children -- Empirical findings on children and divorce -- Effects of differentiated operationalization. Children are an important factor in the stability of marriages. But not every child necessarily increases marital stability: Depending on the relationship between children and their parents, the reduction or increase in marital stability is to be expected. This aspect is less considered in divorce research. Based on the theories of family sociology and the data of the family survey, Andrea Breitenbach examines the influences of different characteristics of children and different marital relationships on marital stability. It shows how relevant theories justify the influence of children on marital stability. The results confirm that depending on childhood relationship and other aspects, contrary directions of the risk of divorce can be observed. Whether in universities, business or politics, everywhere you find mentoring programs as gender-appropriate human resources development, which are intended to counteract the underrepresentation of women in management positions. But what really do mentoring programs bring? This fundamental question is not yet clear in the research to date, the input-output ratio difficult to grasp. Bahar Haghaniprous investigates this question by means of interviews with former participants in a mentoring program. Today, commercial companies use wireless communication technologies such as radio frequency identification (RFID) to optimize warehouse and supply chain management. These technologies are also being tested for automation and individualization of communication with customers within shopping sites. Jens Strüker analyses these new forms of communication and derives operational applications from them. The focus is on the individual customer relationship, which has been characteristic of the "ante-emma-shop" form of operation, but is now also feasible for modern supermarkets. Against the background of intense price competition in the food trade, the considerable revenue potential is shown and discussed in particular on the basis of individualized purchase proposals and monetary incentives for certain customer groups. The author also deals with the limits of a policy of customer-specific treatment by examining and evaluating infrastructure costs and the vulnerability of privacy.
content.title_en: Individualization in stationary retailing : Economic analysis of electronic forms of customer communication

content.text: Prospective effects of cost savings in healthcare on doctors, patients and industry. The rising expenditure in healthcare has led to a variety of cost reduction measures in recent years. Based on standardized surveys, Verena Reichl examines the consequences for doctors, patients and the pharmaceutical and medical engineering industry. The statistical analyses confirm relevant consequences for all investigators. In the case of doctors, the austerity measures lead to a changed regulatory behaviour and in the case of patients they are reflected in payments. Overall, the surveyed persons are prepared to contribute significant sums. It is clear that the doctor as the most important partner of the patient can influence the willingness to participate in his medical treatment. Other relevant explanatory variables are the income structure and the level of education. The study shows the economic consequences of cost savings and gives important insights into the prevailing patient image of the companies
content.title_en: Prospective effects of cost savings in healthcare on doctors, patients and industry

content.text: Georessource Soil — Economic Factor and Ecosystem Service Provider : Recommendations for a bundling of scientific competence in soil and land management. Soil form an essential basis for human life. On them grow plants that serve as food and feed or as biomass, from which energy is derived. They also fulfil important functions in our ecosystem and are a key economic factor as the starting point of all bio-based value chains. Climate change affects both the production and ecosystem functions of the soil. These challenges must also be addressed by research on soil and land management. Acatech POSITION explains why German soil research should work together in a cross-disciplinary manner and identifies eleven necessary and new fields of action for this. acatech provides recommendations on how to combine scientific competence and maintain soil functions. Subject areas and challenges -- The research landscape -- Necessary and new fields of action -- Recommendations.
content.title_en: Georesource Soil — Economic Factor and Ecosystem Service Providers : Recommendations for Pooling Scientific Competence in Soil and Land Management

content.text: In each person, a very personal world emerges in his early childhood. In living with parents, siblings and other people, the consciousness of living in a common reality develops. But how real is this reality? This question approaches the author from the three different perspectives of philosophy, religion and imagination. In philosophy, the 'thing itself' is considered unattainable since Kant. So what is the claim to describe a reality? For believers, the world of faith is profoundly real. How does such a world relate to the worlds of sciences? In imagination, man experiences a reality of the fantastic. What is the significance of this reality in our lives? The author Hans Sillescu has been working as a professor of physical chemistry at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz since 1975. His main research area was the study of extremely slow molecular movements in polymers and in the transition area between highly viscous liquids and amorphous solid bodies. content.text: Why there was no Islamic Middle Ages: the legacy of antiquity and the Orient. Islam has been stuck in the Middle Ages, missed Renaissance, Reformation and Enlightenment. This is the common diagnosis. But what if there was no Islamic Middle Ages? Thomas Bauer shows by numerous examples how ancient times continued in the Islamic world until the 11th century, convincingly refuting the established epoch boundaries and our image of a reform-needed "medieval" Islam. For centuries in the Orient, the ancient cities were alive, with baths, mosques and other stone-built buildings, while in Europe they fell into ruins. Doctors continued Galen's medicine, natural sciences and love poetry flourished. Copper coins, glass, roof tiles, paper: In the daily life of the Orient there were all ancient achievements, which Central Europeans only (again) rediscovered at the beginning of the New Age. Thomas Bauer vividly describes how the ancient culture of al-Andalus continued over North Africa and Syria to Persia and why the 11th century in all Eurasia, the small-scale masterpiece of the Western Europe, the Muslim population, and the Middle-Eastern population soon followed by the Islamic religion.
content.title_en: Why there was no Islamic Middle Ages : the heritage of antiquity and the Orient

content.text: The efficiency of the financial support measures in the new Länder: expert reports. The balance of three years of intensive support policy in the new Länder is mixed. The international competitiveness of East German industry is not yet sufficient. In view of these circumstances, the state support measures are of great importance. The book gives an inventory of the state support policy. In the question of the efficiency of the support measures, model theoretical methods are used on the one hand, and a survey of companies in the new Länder and abroad (Japan) was carried out.

content.text: HEADS, KURS & Co. : Evaluation of surveillance concepts for particularly relapse-prone sex offenders. The monitoring concepts of the federal states aim to protect the general public from relapse-prone sex offenders and violent offenders, which is to be achieved mainly by good cooperation and good information exchange of the participating bodies. Precisely these structures and the procedure within the concepts were evaluated for ten federal states. Since the conceptions of the countries are to preventatively minimize the risk of relapse, a process evaluation offers a good opportunity to investigate the processes carried out towards their efficiency and effectiveness. In a subsequent country comparison, weaknesses and miscontrols are identified in total, in order to submit optimization proposals and initiate further research studies.With contributions by Anja Schiemann, Katharina Büchler, Inge Roith, Ilka Freyhat, Helge Risom, Thomas Heberer, Candy Sommer, Tina Beck, Sven Pahl, Christoph Dümmig, Maik Schröder, Daniel Sühling

content.text: Embedded Controller: Basics and practical implementation for industrial applications. content.text: VIRUS! : Mutations of a metaphor. AIDS, Ebola and crashing computers; foreign bodies, parasites and sleepers; bio- and cyberterrorism, animal diseases and, most recently, SARS: Viruses are currently circulating in a wide variety of areas. The metaphorical of the word is as cross-border and mutating as the concrete objects. It is being sought to enforce threat scenarios and border-securing measures and at the same time serves as a model for resistance and subversive self-stages. No coincidence that the recent media debate about terrorist violence has once again caught up in these patterns. The volume »VIRUS!« examines the effects of the images of risky contacts, contagion and infiltration - not only on the production of »hard facts« in natural sciences and technology, but also on the design of the global world order.
content.title_en: VIRUS! : Mutations of a metaphor

content.text: The basics of data analysis with R: An application-oriented introduction. This book provides an application-oriented introduction to data analysis with the free statistical environment R. It covers descriptive analyses as comprehensively as infertility statistical analyses. In addition to classical univariate methods, the book takes into account nonparametric tests, resampling methods and multivariate statistics. It also covers the many possibilities of preparing data and creating diagrams. The statistical methods are explained by examples and illustrated in many places with diagrams. In the third edition, both the innovations of R 3.1.1 and recent developments in the additional packages have been incorporated. At the same time, the book is being revised and significantly expanded in the areas of logistic regression and crossvalidation. The text now also deals with the ordinary, multinomial and Poisson regression as well as log linear models and the survival analysis. The book is aimed at all those who want to know R and use it in concrete tasks without having to have any previous experience with command-controlled programs or programming languages.
content.title_en: Basics of data analysis with R : An application-oriented introduction

content.text: Real estate valuation with hedonic price models : Theoretical principles and practical application. Real estate valuation with hedonic price models In contrast to traditional real estate valuation, the method of hedonic prices does not depend on the object to be evaluated, but on the information available about the corresponding events and the real estate involved. "According events are e.g. real estate transactions, leases or real estate offers. Using statistical-econometric methods, the hedonic prices of the observable properties of the property are estimated from this information. On the basis of these hedonic prices, concrete objects can be evaluated, i.e. their traffic value. How this happens, is the subject of this book. Because the method of hedonic prices is based on solid statistical bases, it provides additional and, unlike traditional methods, also well-founded information about the quality of the forecast and its spread range. The content Introduction Understanding the data Distribution of Random Variables Regression - the foundations On the search for the best model – Fundamentals On the search for the best model – Example The authors Professor Dr. Gunther Maier is teaching at the Institute of the Regional University of Economics - Sydney.
content.title_en: Real estate valuation with hedonic price models : Theoretical basics and practical application

content.text: Biopolitics. Biopolitics responds to border crossings. It responds to the fact that marginal conditions of human nature, which were previously indisputably applied, become technically available. And it responds to the fact that culturally anchored interpretations of man are challenged by competing scientific concepts. The result are moral controversy and regulatory debates, in which the core question is the old question, whether we can, what we can. Should the new options that offer themselves for the technical handling of man be released? Or should the de facto limits of the ability now replace the limits of moral and legal tolerance? The analyses in this volume aim at this conflict arena and ask for the possible contribution of sociological enlightenment to the questions discussed there.
content.title_en: Biopolitics

content.text: Product planning in the Fuzzy Front End : Action support system based on Fuzzy Cognitive Maps. The Fuzzy Front End, i.e. the early stages of product development, is of central importance for product success. However, conventional methods and procedures of innovation management do not support it. In particular, approaches to systematically taking into account environmental information about markets and technologies and for the exploration, codification and use of existing knowledge are lacking. Antonie Jetter presents a novel Action Support System (HAUS) with which the system "development project" is modelled and its dynamics captured by simulation. The theoretical basis for the HOUSE provides research work of the action psychology. Methodically, the system relies on linked submodels of the development situation, which are created by the qualitative modeling process of the Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs). The construction and use of the HOUSE are concreteized using the example of a real development project and examined for its feasibility.
content.title_en: Product planning in the Fuzzy Front End : Action support system based on Fuzzy Cognitive Maps

content.text: Solutions for linear equation systems : Algorithms and applications. Simulation of technical processes usually requires the solution of linear equation systems of large dimensions. For this purpose, modern pre-conditioned iteration processes (e.g. CG, GMRES, BiCGStab) are derived and the algorithms necessary for the realization are described. For systems with structured matrices efficient direct solution methods are specified. In addition to linear equation systems with block structures, hierarchical matrices for the efficient description and application of fully occupied matrices are also treated. All methods are explained and discussed using simple examples.
content.title_en: Solution methods for linear equation systems : Algorithms and applications

content.text: Reform of the financing of higher education: A financial analysis. 1 Introduction -- 2 Fundamentals of the financing of higher education -- 3 Economic analysis of the financing of higher education -- 4 Design of a private financial participation -- 5 Empirical analysis of the financing of higher education -- 6 Final consideration. Although universities have a significant influence on the competitiveness and technological performance of a country through the training of highly qualified persons, German universities are in a critical state, characterised by, among other things, underfinancing and overfilling. Armin Wiesler examines the necessity and feasibility of reforming the financing of higher education. He analyses whether current funding can be justified by market failures or by distributive considerations, and in this context designs framework conditions and model of private financing participation. Based on an Internet survey, he reviews the attitudes of the population in general and specific groups towards reform of higher education funding. It becomes clear that the introduction of private participation in the costs of higher education from a financial perspective is sensible and politically feasible if the framework conditions of a financing reform are adequately designed.
content.title_en: Reform of the financing of higher education : A financial analysis

content.text: Migration and Family: Historical and Current Analyses. The volume presents studies on the relationship between family and migration in current and historical perspective. content.text: Telecommunications 2017: Building on competition! : Special reports of the Monopoly Commission pursuant to § 121 para. 2 TKG. In its 78th special report entitled "Building on competition!", the Monopoly Commission deals with regulatory and competitive issues in the telecommunications markets. In its report, the Monopoly Commission acknowledges, among other things, the decision of the Federal Network Agency on the use of vectoring technology and discusses the compatibility of so-called zero-rating tariffs with the requirements for net neutrality. The Monopoly Commission also makes proposals to improve the framework conditions for the private and publicly funded expansion of high-performance broadband infrastructures. In addition, the Monopoly Commission takes a position on the current proposals for the re-ordering of the European legal framework for electronic communications.

content.text: The German and Chinese students have been given a PhD in the field of architecture and the rehabilitation of buildings: the examination of conceptual and strategic transmission possibilities. Introduction -- Framework conditions for sustainable renovation -- Overview of rehabilitation projects in Zhejiang -- Overview of the basics and milestone projects in Berlin -- Study of selected sustainable renovation projects in Berlin -- Transferability of the rehabilitation measures to Zhejiang.- Final considerations -- Project register. Ji Zhang discusses the experiences of sustainable renovation of residential buildings in Germany and discusses its transfer possibilities to China. While the renovation of housing in Germany is already well developed, it is still in the beginning in China. The author first gives a brief overview of the framework conditions in both countries, then she analyses 31 outstanding Berlin renovation projects, broken down into five sub-aspects of energy, water, green, building materials and attractiveness. By means of energetic simulation of a reference building and discussions Ji Zhang examines the transferability of the measures applied in Germany to the Hot Summer Cold Winter Zone in China.
content.title_en: Sustainable renovation of residential buildings in Germany and China : Investigation of conceptual and strategic transfer possibilities

content.text: Stakeholder Management: Brief guide Issue 5. This guide shows how a systematic analysis of stakeholders in relation to the performance picture, the honoring and commissioning of project management services in the construction and real estate industry contributes significantly to risk minimisation. In addition to the internal success factors of a project, external influences must also be taken into account. To this end, instructions and tools for analysis and strategy development are presented. Stakeholders of a project in the construction and real estate industry are groups or individuals whose sphere of interest and influence is affected by this project. For the application, the individual project-specific design is necessary, including the project objectives, the marginal conditions to be considered and the specific parameters. This short guide is to be seen in connection with the studies on the performance picture, the honoring and the commissioning of project management services in the construction and real estate industry, as this is recognized as a normative rulebook in project management practice. content.text: Artificial intelligence – When do the machines take over?. Everyone knows them. Smartphones that talk to us, wristwatches that record our health data, workflows that automatically organize themselves, cars, aircraft and drones that control themselves, traffic and energy systems with autonomous logistics or robots that explore distant planets are technical examples of a networked world of intelligent systems. They show us that our everyday life is already determined by AI functions. Biological organisms are also examples of intelligent systems that have emerged in evolution and can solve problems more or less independently efficiently. Occasionally, however, nature is a model for technical developments. Often, however, computer science and engineering science find solutions that are even better and more efficient than in nature. Since their creation, AI research has been linked to great visions about the future of mankind. Does the "artificial intelligence" thus solve people? This book is a plea for engineering: AI must be considered a service in society. Introduction: What is AI? -- A brief history of AI -- Logical thinking becomes automatically -- systems become a social machine?
content.title_en: Artificial intelligence – when do the machines take over?

content.text: The project is a collaborative success in clusters with a network character: An analysis of the success of coordination and relational sources. David Beyer demonstrates multi-theoretically that the design of specific coordination mechanisms at the enterprise and cluster level as well as relational sources at the relationship level significantly determines the success of a cluster. In this context, cluster management as a central coordination unit must define and implement concrete measures to optimally train relational sources. The empirical review is carried out using a structural equation analysis of the responses of 231 companies organized in German clusters. It shows that a successful cluster represents a competitive advantage for the participating companies. content.text: Identity Management in Cloud Computing: Evaluation of Economic and Legal Framework Conditions. Social work, which mainly acts in a district-related manner, is facing an increasing fragmentation of the city and is confronted with the displacement of socially weaker groups. Urban development policy acts as a support and control at the same time: location marketing strengthens the international competitiveness and programs of the district development counteract the collapse of the city. content.text: Insurance and Incentives in the German Welfare State. The concern about the uncertain future and the desire for security unites all people in a country. But state protection also generates misincentives, so that people gain less prosperity and less distribution. Building on a short history of the German welfare state, Charlotte Bartels finds that the protection against income losses is more pronounced than the reduction of income differences. The uncertainty of labour incomes during the reform-intensive past three decades particularly for singles and low earners increased worryingly. Despite the dismantling of various state benefits, the German welfare state guarantees its citizens from 1983 to 2011 a nearly stable income profile, considering income after taxes and transfers. The aim of balancing income differences has been increasingly less and less achieved in the past three decades. The content · Theoretical consideration of insurance by family, market and state · Historical development of welfare state insurance in Germany · Insurance and redistribution of income in Germany and Great Britain · Insurance vs. Work incentives in Germany The target groups · Dozende und Studieren der Wirtschaftslehre und Geschichts · Praktiker in Arbeitsministeriums, Forschungsbehreinrichten und Forschungsbehörung in Deutschland.
content.title_en: Insurance and incentives in the German welfare state

content.text: Business Analytics: Effective use of advanced algorithms in corporate management. Using data to solve business problems effectively and efficiently. The importance of business analytics derives directly from the rapidly increasing availability of data resulting from the digitalization of all areas of life. But how do companies now translate this data into better products, new services, innovative business models or, more generally, better business decisions? In order to address the challenges structured, this book presents a business analytics process that is divided into the four sub-processes framing, allocation, analytics and preparation. It is the basis for developing and implementing a business-individual business analytics approach. Numerous real business examples provide inspiration for concrete approaches in their own companies: from the procurement of data through the selection of the optimal algorithm to the recipient-oriented visualization of results. On these questions, managers of the middle and top management of all industries find answers in this book. It supports in identifying urgent problems of business management and solving them using data. How is the placement of central algorithms in the focus of the business?
content.title_en: Business Analytics : Effective use of advanced algorithms in corporate management

content.text: Perception - Cognition - Aesthetics : Neurobiology and Media Science. Perception, cognition and aesthetics can be understood as different forms of processing and expression of a basic biological equipment of man. Whether these are stable or whether they are culturally overformed or even transformed, forms the central media anthropological question of the volume. In this process, it is examined what kind of reciprocal impulses are, which can lead to cultural and biological changes, what effect they have and what duration they have. These questions are not directed solely at processes of perception, cognitive or aesthetic habituation, but rather at the physiological conditions. With the participation of proven researchers from the fields of biology, medicine and brain research, this volume opens up Neuland in the border area of natural and cultural sciences.
content.title_en: Perception - Cognition - Aesthetics : Neurobiology and Media Studies

How we develop, change and disseminate knowledge today differs in many ways from earlier forms. The extensive volume provides a current inventory of the different dimensions of the internet-based knowledge society. In more than 50 contributions, practitioners, journalists and scientists take stock of politics and economics, education, media and art, and thus compare discussion and reality.

content.text: How to unmask a chocolate thief : ... and other mathematical magic tricks. This book introduces you to the world of logic and mathematics with amazing magic tricks and comic clowneries. Numbers and spaces become a fascinating world of magic, flunking and laughter. Because, even if you hardly believe it, mathematics is ripe for the stage and charmingly beautiful. How can you finally get this sneaky chocolate thief on the edge? How do monks with a vow of silence find out who is sick of them? And is there really a trick to find his lady of hearts? This book contains lovingly designed detailed instructions on how to tinker and solve such puzzles – ideal for parents, grandparents, teachers and children. The author Carla Cederbaum studied mathematics, physics and computer science in Freiburg and Cambridge and received her doctorate in mathematics in 2011 in Berlin. In addition to her research and teaching in mathematics, she is also active in science communication and has been awarded several times for this. Since 2016 she has been Professor of Mathematics in Tübingen and received the 2017 Student School of Mathematics - Student's Award for Mathematics.

content.text: The virtual society of the 21st century: Social change in the digital age. "No stone will remain on the other", says the prognosis of Heidelberg sociologist Achim Bühl on the social consequences of modern information and communication technologies. A relevant part of human life will be played out in cyberspace in the near future. This thesis is clearly and understandable for the field of work, production and distribution of goods and communication. The second edition of the work has been completely revised and greatly expanded. New additions are the chapters social structure, gender relations, law and the individual of virtual society. The transition from the industrial to the "information society" is now comprehensively illustrated. The challenges for politics and economics, culture and education, but also for the everyday life of the individual, are clearly illustrated.
content.title_en: The virtual society of the 21st century: Social change in the digital age

content.text: The cost-effective and efficient construction operation is characterized by the optimal use of the equipment in a process chain for the respective specified construction work tasks. The performance determination is the basis of a systematic and result-oriented calculation and construction site preparation of the greatest importance. This manual is intended to serve as reference work and formula collection for both students and practitioners in the AV and calculation of construction companies. It can be used to perform performance determinations in the construction enterprise. An analytical basic concept for the performance determination of construction equipment as well as the process chains of parallel and successively switched devices of different subprocesses is presented. In this case, usually no "standard values" are specified, but only the elementary analytical connections. In the annex, the reader finds on a CD-ROM the usual standard devices with technical information, which are usually sufficient in the supply phase and for the preparation of a construction site. Thus, the annex of the manual can serve as a machine-technical reference work in the construction enterprise at the same time.
content.title_en: Performance determination for construction machinery and processes

content.text: In this guide, Hans Bürkle, the Nestor of career consulting in Germany, presents his successful application methods and advice especially for the engineer from 40.
