content.text: Digitality in school and teaching: a guide to practice: all levels of school. The social pressure on schools to develop digital teaching offers has increased – not least due to the Corona crisis. In many places, the technical possibilities for digital teaching need to be created or further developed. However, even where presentation media and end devices are available, suitable digital communication platforms are needed that are appropriate to the needs of the school's assignment and everyday school life. Moreover, schools build concepts that can deal with digital forms of communication. Moreover, the media skills of teachers and learners have not been systematically developed in recent years. The book is aimed at all participants in the process of redesigning our schools. It brings transparency into the complex set of conditions, from social pressure, educational objectives and the options for action of individual schools, which are very different. This is not about contributing to the social, political and educational-didactic discourse, but about the perspectives for the design and development of school practice in times of digitalization.

content.text: 8. The AI in the job: Guide to successful human-machine collaboration. content.text: Autonomy and responsibility in digital cultures: privateness in the web of law, media and society. The increasing complexity of networked systems raises fundamental doubts about self-determination in digital. Foreign-determining algorithms and practices of self- and foreign-dates raise questions about protection and endangering autonomy and freedom of opinion. Nevertheless, the legal, political, ethical, social and economic responsibility for the consequences of digital transformation processes for societies, collectives and individuals remains unexplained. In this field of tension, this interdisciplinary band wants to stimulate a discussion on responsibilities and impact assessments. Problems within digital cultures are explored, possible control possibilities discussed and conflicts of economic, political and social systems discussed. With contributions by Anna K. Bernzen, Barbara Büttner & Carsten Ochs, Stephan Dreyer, Hans-Christian Gräfe & Andrea Hamm, Hermann Jakobi & Elizaveta Saponchik, Thomas Krämer-Badoni & Jens Crueger, Wulf Loh, Tim Raupach & Phillip Siedenburg, Caroline Richter & Christian Lenk, Alexander Schär, Julia Schröder Witt

content.text: New work and digital natives are the current keywords. A few years ago, it was assumed that employees need a strong hand, that they need a clear goal and, above all, the way to it. The new leadership approaches, however, take into account that certain freedoms and independent action can lead to the specified goal more efficiently. Classical leadership theories and concepts combine leadership success primarily with the behaviour and characteristics of the superior. New approaches, on the other hand, allow a broader perspective on leadership by focusing more on the interaction process between managers and employees, the importance of employees and the organizational context. The author not only explains the differences between the classic leadership approaches and the New Work concepts, but also shows how both "worlds of leadership" can be reconciled.
content.title_en: Human Resources Management in Digital Change : from the classic leadership approaches to the New Work concepts

content.text: Building with paper : Architecture and construction. The natural material paper is currently the subject of research and testing in construction practice. The focus of the use is on temporary use, for example in transition buildings for schools, emergency shelters or microhomes. content.text: Hegau : Geology of the Volcanic Landscape between Danube and Lake Constance. "This new volume from the collection of geological guides combines proven and new. It is a completely new and substantially expanded version of volume 62 of the Geological Guide 'Hegau and Lake Constance to the west' (1976). Under new title 'Hegau - Geology of the Volcanic Landscape between Danube and Lake Constance', he describes the geological structure and the history of the development of the extensive volcanic landscape of the Hegau region, between the southern edge of the Swabian Alb and the Upper Danube to the north-western Lake Constance. The characteristic volcanic cones, among them the well-known Hohentwiel near Singen, are the erosion and glacial over-presence of former volcanic structures. The introductory part, after short references to vegetation, soil science and archaeology, convey a detailed description of the geological conditions and the rocks found in the Hegau. A reference to natural hazards and the raw material situation complete it. Below, 63 excursion points are described; additional to this, the position of natural causes are added to the various excursion points.

content.text: Geography is destiny: Power struggle between Britain, Europe and the world - a 10,000-year history. Who are we, where do we live, what do we have, how do we protect ourselves and who does the rules? These questions have always been driving humanity around, and they are all determined by the geographical situation. This is shown by historian, archaeologist and best-selling author Ian Morris with a view to Britain, the former empire. He tells the story of his changing relations with Europe and the world, from the physical separation at the end of the Ice Age to the first beginnings of the United Kingdom, the struggles around the Atlantic Ocean and the rise of the Pacific region.Based on maps, images and latest archaeological finds, Morris examines how geography, migration, politics and new technologies worked together and produced inequalities that are still characteristic to the present day. Where does Britain and where does Europe stand when the world stage is moving eastward? A global challenge, as shown in a flash glass. Ian Morris is considered a pioneer when it comes to making world history interesting and understandable?
content.title_en: Geography is fate : Power struggle between Britain, Europe and the world - a 10 000-year history

content.text: Chemistry of biology : Basis and origin of evolution. The material basis of all living organisms are chemical compounds, which are usually composed of several elements. The periodic table of elements, in which the elements are arranged in a characteristic structure, contains a small number of artificially produced elements besides the 94 naturally occurring elements. In nature there is only a small part of these elements, besides carbon, it is mainly oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur and a few metals. This results from the electron affinities, ionization energies, electronegativity, oxidation numbers and the geometry of the associated compounds. This also results in the presence of the various natural substances, their reaction possibilities and thus ultimately also the evolution. The authors, a professor of organic chemistry and a teaching force for chemistry didactics, want to put the fundamental role of chemistry in the center with their book. A short appendix includes literature notes and a factual register. - recommended for students and teachers of natural sciences.

content.text: Modelling the expertise of teachers in particle physics (volume 315). Particle physics as a sub-area of modern physics is becoming increasingly important in school physics teaching. In this work, the knowledge required by teachers is modelled for the first time on particle physics, whereby expertise is understood as part of the profession knowledge. As a focus on the content areas and the types of knowledge, for which subfacets are identified and precisely described.After a review of the essential ideas of particle physics, the work presents the successive modelling of the expertise in a qualitative and quantitative Delphi study. content.text: The unequal university: diversity, excellence and anti-discrimination. Continuing inequality among students, barriers to university professorships, growing precarization among young academics: universities are in permanent criticism – despite scientific and university reform measures, or precisely because of that? Universities are more than institutions for education and research. Socially, they also bear responsibility for promoting social justice and social inclusive structures. Current university reforms have given university leaders more power of design. Nevertheless, equality is only slowing down, and anti-discrimination measures are not sufficient to open universities socially and culturally sustainably. In addition to established power structures, the reasons for this are the developments promoted in the context of scientific and high-school reform efforts such as excellence policies, competitive orientation and deregulation of employment. These developments contribute to a sharper struggle for good work and professional prospects at universities. Here again, those groups that have been clearly underrepresented since time immemorially. The book refers to these developments and leads to current high-school-related debates on sexism, racism and professional perspectives.
content.title_en: The uneven university : diversity, excellence and anti-discrimination

content.text: The BIM method is used in sustainable construction: the status quo of applications in practice. The integration of sustainability requires a paradigm shift in the life cycle of buildings. By using the BIM method, aspects of sustainable construction can be integrated more strongly into processes and workflows. Information is recorded across life cycle, consistent and structured and made available to all involved. This essential defines the status quo of applications for the application of the BIM method in sustainable construction. content.text: Perfect 3D prints with Simplify3D. This textbook provides a sound and practical introduction to the topic of electromagnetic compatibility. Due to increasing circuit complexity, increasing integration density and higher frequency signal components, the requirements for developers grow if they want to present a technically flawless and electromagnetically compatible product. The book shows which technical requirements to meet, which methods can be used to analyse coupling paths and which interference measures are possible. The aim is to provide a comprehensive overview. Initially, the physical-technical phenomena of influence are discussed in detail. The focus is on the field-theoretical tool for analyzing and optimizing the EMC of a device. Subsequently, the authors describe the verification by the laboratory test and the underlying standard landscape including its complex approval processes. From the content: basics and concepts, spreading of interference signals, components and concepts for improving the EMC, guidelines, norms and approval processes.
content.title_en: Perfect 3D prints with Simplify3D

content.text: Social robotics: a social science introduction. The textbook provides a systematic, social science introduction to social robotics. This sub-area of research into artificial intelligence aims to develop human-like robots that are intended to enter into social relations with people. Three parts shed light on the most important aspects of social robotics. The first part focuses on the history of AI research, illuminates the 'dream' of artificial humans and finally traces how sociology has been observing the topic since the 1980s. The second part opens up a sociological perspective on the production of social robots in the laboratories of engineering sciences and the social consequences of the development and establishment of social robots. Finally, the third part focuses on social theoretic perspectives that address the question of sociality of social robots and show how this question can be answered by means of exemplary case studies.
content.title_en: Social robotics: a social science introduction

content.text: Cultural Sociological Urban Research: Basics, Analyses, Perspectives. This volume formulates the basics of urban research conceived in a sociological way. The focus is on how a cultural-scientific view of cities can help to re-answer classic questions of urban sociology. Through the focus of their analysis on key cultural structural categories such as gender, class and race, the authors succeed in expanding the sociological debate on the topic of city by a feminist and postcolonial perspective. Furthermore, their reflections show how a cultural sociological approach can help to analyze cities in the context of current social and ecological challenges.
content.title_en: Cultural Sociological Urban Research : Basics, Analyses, Perspectives

content.text: Care work spatial thinking : feminist perspectives on planning and development. Describes the situation in Switzerland. The thesis of this book is that care and a "caring" attitude produce other forms of living together, of business and household, other forms of private, political and entrepreneurial action in this world, and that these in turn involve other institutional, built and spatial structures.
content.title_en: Care work spatial thinking : feminist perspectives on planning and development

content.text: Gender differences in educational context: from scientific studies to impulses for teaching practice. Are girls more motivated in reading? Are boys more interested in mathematics? Again and again studies show gender differences in interest, motivation and career plans of pupils – and this has social implications: more men than women in STEM professions, unused potential, wage inequality. But how do these differences arise, which have such a great impact on important life decisions? And what can teachers, school leaders and other actors contribute to educational practice to reduce gender differences? The subject book examines these and other questions. To begin with, the authors provide detailed theoretical background information on the causes of gender differences and their occurrence in student characteristics such as interest and motivation. The core of the issue is a synthesis of research that deals with the promotion of these characteristics. Here, the authors analyse the extent to which the impact of the support measures for girls and boys differs and from which students benefit most in general.
content.title_en: Gender differences in educational context: from scientific studies to impulses for teaching practice

content.text: Adult education in an international perspective: Limits and opportunities. The volume deals in two ways with the internationalization and internationality of adult education. On the one hand, an internal perspective on the research landscape is taken by the fact that specific internationalization phenomena of adult and further education find a contextualized presentation. On the other hand, externally induced research questions are addressed and discussed under the perspective of their internationality. The contributors make visible both reactive and anticipative movements and dynamics as well as opportunities and limits of internationalization. This volume addresses internationalization and internationality of adult education in two ways. On the one hand, it takes an internal perspective on the research landscape by contextualized specific phenomena of internationalization in adult education and learning. On the other hand, externally induced research questions are addressed from the perspective of their internationality. Both-reactive and anticipatory dynamics as well as limitations of internationalization.
content.title_en: Adult education in an international perspective : Limits and opportunities

content.text: About mobility: Historical aspects of techniques, cultures and utopias of movement. The history of mobility in the 20th century has always been characterised by fascination and hope for the future. Kurt Möser's essayist texts show this for many aspects of automotive mass motorization as well as for amphibious vehicles or electric airships. His cultural-historical perspective strongly explains why mobility cannot be reduced to the formula, how one gets from A to B at a low price. Möser's case studies illustrate how emotionally charged the use of mobility machines has always been - and indeed also in terms of their "dark" aggressive sides. The long line of mobility history, as it is developed here, provokes doubts as to whether current concepts for a mobility turn adequately take into account the cultural dimension of mobility.
content.title_en: About Mobility : Historical about techniques, cultures and utopias of transportation

content.text: Social policies against poverty. Even if the consequences of the unification have not least worsened the framework conditions for effective poverty prevention and poverty reduction, alternative strategies for a needs-based poverty policy are now more urgent than ever. The contributions of this volume focus on the analysis of traditional structural deficits and the changing framework conditions for social policy interventions on the poverty problem at national and local level. On the other hand, they outline strategic approaches and instruments for a more effective policy on poverty reduction and avoidance for various social policy areas and discuss their conditions and implications.
content.title_en: Social policies against poverty

content.text: Digital Capital in Use : an Ethnography on the Transformation of Digital Practices in Art Education. For some time now, the education at art universities has been increasingly discussing questions about the relationship between digital and analogue practices, between technical know-how and artistic idea, as well as between university offerings and individual orientations for action. Using theses in art, design and art mediation, the authors investigate which digital practices students use, on which skills and knowledge they use and how their use is evaluated. In this way, they show potential connections between the discourse on digital transformation and the educational opportunities of art students.
content.title_en: Digital Capital in Use: an Ethnography on the Transformation of Digital Practices in Art Education

content.text: The volume includes the educational scientific discussions and research perspectives that open up in the tension between normalization and pathologisation within the school. Considerations and studies on processes of individualization or social debates on school heterogeneity and social inequality are included here as well as the relevance of medical-psychiatric and psychological discourses for pedagogy. This results in diverse questions on general aspects of educational science in the context of conceptual education, the (ethical and political) discussion about participation, equal opportunities or educational equity as well as current debates about the institution of school and education systems – for example in the context of inclusion – and about understanding of professions.
content.title_en: School and pathology

content.text: Professional recognition in the system of institutional day care for children: contexts, processes, evaluation. Recognition of qualifications acquired abroad is seen as an important tool in current scientific and policy debates to remedy the shortage of skilled workers in day care for children. However, the challenges associated with this have so far been examined only marginally in the specialist discussion. The volume starts here and addresses the recognition of international degrees in the field of day care for children in different contexts and from different perspectives, which largely result from the evaluation of the project »Vielfalt welcome« of the Robert Bosch Stiftung.
content.title_en: Professional recognition in the system of institutional day care for children : contexts, processes, evaluation

content.text: Knowledge-based science, how to use knowledge in the enterprise with the help of artificial intelligence, and how to use knowledge in the enterprise. The future workplace is increasingly shaped by knowledge work. Knowledge-based science deals with concepts, methods and processes for systematically generating, extracting, storing and providing knowledge to solve problems, and can thus be assigned to knowledge management. Cognitive assistants ensure that the right knowledge is provided at the right time in the right way to their users. In order to achieve this, numerous methods of artificial intelligence (AI) are now used to support different tasks of knowledge management. The contentHow can AI methods support knowledge-based knowledge-based knowledge-based knowledge-based management in companies? This book characterizes the workplace of the future and highlights the importance of knowledge and its management. The aim is not to replace people with AI, but to use cognitive assistants to best support them in their work. Which areas of the enterprise can be optimized or completely transformed by artificial intelligence methods? Which steps are both organizationally and technically necessary and how individual methods are actually used in this field of knowledge analysis?
content.title_en: Knowledge Science – Case Studies : How Artificial Intelligence Supports Knowledge Security and Use in the Company

content.text: In the last 20 years, new forms of cooperation have been developed in the framework of youth assistance with »coordination centres«, »partnerships« and »interdisciplinary advisory bodies« in various cities and counties. They aim to establish sustainable working alliances in the helper system on the one hand and to develop flexible settings that the young people can endure. Often, innovative projects are also created in this context, which enrich the youth support landscape. In the book, practitioners present the organizational models they have developed, report on the cross-media work on cases and show innovative effects of these cooperations with a view to the youth support structures. The editorial team reflects and comments on the contributions. Renowned scientists contribute the results of their first evaluations.
content.title_en: Crisis in educational aid: cooperation, risk partnerships, responsibility communities

content.text: Biographies in Germany: sociological reconstructions of lived social history. German contemporary history in the 20th century is also the history of the appropriation of the various forms of society in life stories. The emergence of social and state systems, their transformation and decline is supported and reflected in biographies in Germany. The collection combines research work of sociological biography research and discussions immediately after the unification of Germany by scientists from the old and new federal states.
content.title_en: Biographies in Germany : sociological reconstructions of lived social history

content.text: Individual action and common good : an interdisciplinary theory of action in the context of freedom, responsibility and artificial intelligence. In the case of conflicts in the private or professional context and in social or military conflicts, there are always certain questions: Why does someone do something like this? What motives and thoughts play a role in this? Could another action have improved or prevented the situation? Gerhard Tulodziecki designs an interdisciplinary theory of action to get closer to answering such questions. In this context, it is also about freedom of decision and responsibility in action - also in view of the increasing use of artificial intelligence. Thus, there are various suggestions for the assessment of action in everyday life, occupation and politics as well as for the reflection of one's own action.
content.title_en: Individual action and common good : an interdisciplinary theory of action in the context of freedom, responsibility and artificial intelligence

content.text: The AI was! : from absurd to deadly: the pitfalls of artificial intelligence. That algorithms decide about people and their future seems inevitable - we are all long ago exposed to the judgments of artificial intelligence: more and more companies are automatically evaluating applications, and more and more people are getting information or information prepared by machines. However, not all of these algorithmic decisions are correct, there are always cases in which AI discriminates, innocents are accused of a crime or even endanger life. Katharina Zweig, a widely excellent computer science professor, explains entertainingly and with exciting current cases how we can recognize wrong decisions and resist them. Because we should know what we need to be careful about, so that algorithms play according to our rules and not according to their own. Where artificial intelligence is mistaken and why it is committed to us allGermany's leading socio-informatics specialist explains by means of many examples of our everyday life, how we can recognize false software decisions - and how we can resist them 2023 will be able to adopt the artificial intelligence act at EU level - and how the digitally-based branch should be adopted by us - 25.
content.title_en: The AI was : from absurd to lethal: the pitfalls of artificial intelligence

content.text: Building sites of the nation: what we have to change now in Germany. It crumbles at the foundations of our state. Whether with the degraded infrastructure, the catastrophic deficits in the education sector or the little-hearted energy transition: Germany has slept and slowed down reforms and investments for years. Philip Banse and Ulf Buermeyer describe the most important problems and outline solutions: What must happen to ensure that the wind power expansion finally succeeds? How do we catch up with the backlog in digitisation? How do we make sure that Germany's roads and schools no longer literally crumble, that the railways function reliably again and that the pensions are finally really safe?
content.title_en: Building sites of the nation: what we need to change now in Germany

content.text: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning with R: Applications in the field of business analytics. In a VUCA world that proves to be increasingly unstable, uncertain and more complex, it is important for companies, organizations and states to respond promptly and adequately to the respective situations. Making decisions based on past experiences is less successful than an accurate understanding of the current conditions in these times. The importance of empirical sciences, the permanent observation of the environment, the timely analysis of effects and the resulting gain of new insights is increasing. From this it is possible to derive which measures are suitable with a predictable probability for achieving their own goals, e.g. the price of an offer generates the desired demand or the marketing measure reaches a desired target group. Where classical statistics for calculations and predictions were used earlier, today allow free (open source) tools such as R data in various formats and from any number of sources for analysis, for example, to be read and analyzed with the help of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods. Where classical statistics were used for calculations and predictions, the results can then be perfectly visualized by the use of the term of the term, and the term of the term of the term is effectively achieved by means of the term of the term.
content.title_en: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning with R : Applications in Business Analytics

content.text: All and nothing to say: the state of debate in digital modernism. Is a liberal society pulling away the ground on which it should stand? An essay on what digital mass communication does to people in the interpersonal world. Nothing has changed living together as extensively as digitalisation – we think, feel and argue differently since we are permanently connected and overinformed. The effects affect everyone, no matter how much they use the new media at all. It is a stress test for society: the abundance of knowledge, speed, transparency and indelibility is unchannelled, no value in itself. Democracy-politically important this becomes in the much-intoxicated debate culture. Because the forms of dealing with the so-called social media have long since passed over the other arenas, politics and journalism play already according to the new, merciless rules. Previously recognized authorities are being cleared up in the dozen without new ones coming after the better argument, because the narrow delegitimization of the opponent has been replaced by the short-terms. A functioning public – as a marketplace of opinions and place of social clarification – there seems to be a break in Eva's, and an essay, and a lot of questions are still being addressed.
content.title_en: All and nothing to say : the state of debate in digital modernism

content.text: Technology as consolation : promises of artificial intelligence. Promises of artificial intelligence (AI) are speculative ascriptions of meaning and promises of salvation that make AI a collective comfort project - according to Stefan Selke. In a meta-study he compares four prototypical narratives of the future and draws on sources from technical texts to science fiction. His socio-scientific 360-degree view of the opaque phenomenon AI makes clear: promises play a central role in the future, technically shaped world design. Thanks to the innovative approach to the subject, not only scientists are addressed, but all those who have an interest in AI and other transformational topics as well as an expansion of the discourse.
content.title_en: Technology as comfort : promises of artificial intelligence

content.text: New Networking: the smart way to digital visibility and sovereign networks. Wake-up call, encouragement and guidance for better visibility in self-determined work and networks. Beautiful new (working) world? Rather not. Kathrin Koehler often experiences reservations in her coachings about the "self-presentation" on internal and external digital platforms such as LinkedIn, Instagram, etc. She hears the voices of the inner critics: inside and she experiences over-stress and discouragement day after day. Therefore, her mission is to encourage the new working world as well as the communication channels associated with it to understand as an opportunity for personal development and to use as a stage of professional communication. In this book Kathrin Koehler directs the context of New Work and New Networking and explores in interviews the overcoming of blockages, smart tactics for introverted, content development and design, time management, handling with multi-consistency by a multitude of active networkers in the company and much more. She then takes the reader: in a step-by-step guide for better professional positioning with a learning journey to develop the new network potential in the process of communicating and communicating.
content.title_en: New Networking: the smart way to digital visibility and sovereign networks

content.text: Historical production logics of technical knowledge : Helmut Maier on his 65th birthday. The contributions gathered in this volume are dedicated to Helmut Maier on his 65th birthday. Maier has opened up pioneering perspectives for the history of technology, the environment and science with numerous widely received monographs and manuals. This applies especially to his fundamental research on the history of the engineering sciences in the first half of the 20th century and his interest in specific and collective biographies of the actors involved. content.text: Optics. The standard work of optics for over 25 years: Readers appreciate this textbook mainly because of its balanced didactic concept. It explains the mathematics of wave movement in an easily understandable way and deals in detail with both classical and modern methods of optics. The author's aim is to standardize the optics within the framework of a few, overarching concepts, so that students get a coherent picture in themselves. The 8th edition is rounded off by numerous, didactically excellently prepared illustrations and many current photos. Over 800 exercise tasks of various difficulty levels, which are largely available with complete solutions, enable the student to independently check his knowledge.

content.text: Cities are starting off at the road. Places and cities have developed along roads. In recent decades, the constant expansion of motorized individual traffic and the structural response to its noise have strongly shaped the spatial structure along the roads and, in many places, together with the lack of quality of residence have led to inhospitable urban spaces. This finding is based on urban development starting at the road and is trying to remedy it. The book, which has emerged from many years of research by the Institute Urban Landscape of the ZHAW in Winterthur, shows ways in which the roads become a backbone of local and urban development from the problem case. Using analyses and photo documentation, today's qualities and challenges are discussed. With concrete examples from Switzerland, Germany and Austria, the book shows strategies on how the challenges of climate adaptation, mobility, noise and the relation to the district structure can be thought integrally and roads can become quality-filled public spaces again.
content.title_en: Urban planning starts at the road

content.text: Ethicals of the appropriation: cultural appropriation. Is this to be understood as over-grid, even racist – especially when profit is being made from it? Again and again prominent artists and artists, but also persons in their everyday activities, are accused of using the cultural property of other groups, usually marginalized. What basic assumptions are behind this accusation, and how can it be assessed? Jens Balzer shows that both sides often make themselves too easy in this debate. Thus, those who raise the accusation of cultural appropriation would often have little understanding that any culture is based on hybridity and practices of appropriation. content.text: Digital transformation is not only a technological challenge, it is a pervasive process and the overall organisation of the hospital: diagnostics and therapy, processes and procedures, documentation and communication will change radically. In addition to numerous opportunities, digital transformation also involves risks that require new rules of play in the handling of data and technology. Not least, uncertainties arise when assessing and solving difficult decision-making situations – not only in technical but also in ethical and legal dimensions. "Digital hospital" provides the responsible persons with tools for action and knowledge to optimally shape the process of change. Accordingly, technological basic knowledge is conveyed as well as the entire practical knowledge for all relevant areas in which decisions about the implementation of IT infrastructure and process modifications can be made, as well as investment and personnel decisions. In addition, digital transformation is also addressed in its social, ethical, psychological and not least economic dimension. By its very nature, data protection and information security, including the legal regulations as well as the influence of digitalization on the role of the patients and their digitalisation, requires a high degree of behaviour and participation.
content.title_en: The Digital Hospital

content.text: General schools in migration society: diversity-sensitive approaches and perspectives. The second volume of the series "Migration, Diversity and Education" outlines current challenges for the field of action of general schools in migration society and derives scientific, educational and educational policy choices from them. The volume provides an overview of central current discourse fields as well as empirical findings in individual fields of action, on topics such as the representation of migration-social aspects in the curricula, the social relevance of teacher formation, on racialism-critical perspectives on language, on the transnationality of pupils and the need to take into account various religious-world-viewal orientations of young people in schools.

content.text: Integral leadership skills : Action strategies for uncertain times. How can the effectiveness of a media didactics be determined, what are the aspects and criteria of effective media didactics and how can they be legitimized? content.text: Joint task Climate protection in schools : a guide : with e-book inside. This book offers a guide for more climate protection in schools and brings school leaders, teachers and pupils: in the boat together – because climate protection is a joint task. The »Whole School Approach« initiates the holistic implementation of climate protection activities in school development and facilitates them at school level. The aim is to strengthen teachers: in their design skills for more climate protection – this is done by concrete proposals for working with pupils: in schools. Participative methods of participation are to give pupils: empower and teachers ideas to increase their own self-effectiveness, but also those of the students: inside. The central message is: a climate protection project at school is essential for the structural anchoring of education for sustainable development in school life. The guide gives • suggestions for teaching design • suggestions for the development of a climate protection guide image, • instructions for building management, • ideas for the integration of the school environment.
content.title_en: Joint task Climate protection in schools : a guide : with e-book inside

content.text: Review of Facility Management : An audit guide. Facility management covers the entire life cycle of buildings and related outdoor facilities. Vulnerabilities in operation or late integration into the design of real estate can quickly affect the costs of investment, use and operation. This guide, developed by the DIIR working group "Construction, operation and maintenance", systematically looks at the many audit approaches to facility management: - Governance and operator responsibility, IKS and risk management - Technical building management: Technical object management, maintenance, conversions and modernizations, energy management, supply and disposal - Infrastructural building management: Cleaning, outdoor facilities, security, area management and other services - Commercial building management: Contracts and procurement, controlling, insurance, etc. The all-round updated 2nd edition of the practical book supports you with many hundred possible audit questions on all risk-relevant areas.
content.title_en: Review of Facility Management : An Audit Guide

content.text: Object-Oriented Software Development with UML. - For all those who want to deal with the workings of software development - Compact representation of object-oriented basic principles - Use of the current standard of UML - Discussion of agile and collaborative methods - Additional material: Solutions to the tasks; Source code in Java, C#, Eiffel, Pascal and Python; All images and interesting links - Your exclusive advantage: E-Book inside when buying the printed book The book provides an introduction to the object-oriented specification with UML (Unified Modeling Language), a standard for object-oriented software development. In addition to the use of the language elements of UML, methods for user-centric software development are presented and discussed. This starts with the analysis of requirements and their specification by scenarios and application case models. The idea of the design patterns is presented and the notation possibilities in UML are discussed. Examples of much used design patterns and their application in programming are supplemented by the content. Both state and activity diagrams are presented in detail. In addition, possibilities are also shown how the D-Input and Insurance are not listed in the UML-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-Input-In.
content.title_en: Object-oriented software development with UML

content.text: Climate change in Germany: Development, consequences, risks and perspectives. This open access book describes the impact of climate change on the economy and society in Germany. It provides a well-founded, interdisciplinary basis for decisions in relation to climate change. How can we mitigate the consequences of climate change and how can we prepare ourselves? The national study presented here presents the current state of research on climate change comprehensively for all topics and social sectors. A total of 165 authors from all over the German-speaking world express themselves in 39 chapters on topics such as observed and future changes, weather disasters and their consequences. Expectations for the future, opportunities and risks as well as possible adaptation strategies are identified in tangible, open questions. Five chapters on mitigation and zero emission strategies show further possible ways out of the situation. The texts are written in comprehensible language and the most important thoughts are illustrated by graphics and tables. All contributions have been scientifically assessed several times. With the 2nd, revised and extended edition of climate change in Germany, the first comprehensive review on the topic complex from 2017 was updated and improved, seven chapters were added. The work focuses on a readership of the basic understanding of all the activities of climate change and the German economy.
content.title_en: Climate change in Germany : Development, consequences, risks and perspectives

content.text: Between the port and the horizon: world history of the seas. Here, historian North presents a 3,000-year history of seafaring on the oceans. The overview is supplemented by chapters on "Dangers and Endangers" (cruising, overfishing and fertilisation). Review: North is a historian at the University of Greifswald. With this hardcover he presents a 3,000-year-long history of seafaring. He has assigned individual chapters to the various world seas, supplemented by those on globalization and "Dangers and Endangers" (cruising, tanker, overfertilization and fishing). Unlike, for example, S. Winchester: "The Atlantic" (2012), this publication is prosaic and without excursions to other scientific disciplines. The text is generally understandable and satisfies scientific demands (sources, registers). The book provides a good overview, hardly refers to individual famous ships, explorers or sea wars. Black-white illustrations and maps are taken from the volume. The image material goes right to the present (the bathing guests are present).
content.title_en: Between the port and the horizon : World history of the seas

content.text: Politics with memory: Memorial sites in the dispute over the Nazi past. Public memory of the Nazi era is often controversial, especially when it is fixed on symbols such as memorial sites, memorial sites or rituals of memorial days; sometimes a dispute with sharpness and bitterness, such as the recent Holocaust memorial in Berlin. The Hamburg political scientist examines such a dispute about the memory culture on selected examples and thus draws on his book "Der schöne Schein des Thirte Reichs" (BA 8/91). Monuments: among others Krieger- und Antikriegsdenkmal Hamburg, Börneplatz Frankfurt; memorials: KZ Buchenwald, Dachau, Neuengamme u.a.; memorial sites: Berlin with Wannsee-Villa, Neuer Wache, Deutschem Historisches Museum etc.; memorial days: calendar memory and political scandals. Brisant current report on a central piece of German life and consciousness history. (2)
content.title_en: Politics with memory : Memorial sites in the struggle over the Nazi past

content.text: Your poverty is puking us! : Solidarity in the crisis. Klappentext: With the growth euphoria of the economic miracle years, the instruments of the welfare state have also come into crisis. No one was prepared for mass poverty and permanent unemployment. The reactions are often fantasies and heartless (site debate, dismantling of the welfare state) or even brutal ("Get out of sight! Your poverty is puking us!). This volume looks for answers that respond with ingenuity and sense of responsibility to the current crisis of solidarity.
content.title_en: Your poverty is puking us! : Solidarity in the crisis

content.text: The main features of the parking plan are: (i) the financing and management of parking spaces (ii) the promotion and financing of university parking spaces (iii) the calculation of the full cost of parking spaces (iii) the management of university parking spaces (including the function and effects of parking space management). (iv) the basics of the parking plans at universities (iii) the planning and approval procedures for the local authority (iv) the standard design procedure (iv) the building-related measurement and the design according to the balance of the location 5. the different design procedures 6. the special situation in the new countries). - Part D. the country reports (PHF/ Übern.)
content.title_en: Pitching at universities : basics of building regulations and their handling

content.text: Pollutants in the environment: chemical bases for the assessment of air, water and soil pollution. A textbook that, carefully worked on for German conditions, transports up-to-date data and investigation techniques. It deals mainly with basics: transport and behaviour of pollutants in the environment, their analysis and monitoring as well as, in the main part, the individual inorganic and organic pollutants with their chemical properties and toxic effects in air, water, soil. It also contains a short outline of German pollutant law and a separate chapter from U. Förster on common environmental analysis methods (reduction and avoidance of pollutant emissions). Clearly structured, with many tables and graphs. - In addition to C. B, "Environmental Chemistry" (BA 5/95) and A. Heintz: "Chemistry and Environment" (4th edition: BA 6/96). Especially indispensable for libraries at university sites. (2) (Helga Lüdtke) presents the organic and inorganic pollutants with their chemical properties and toxic effects; together with an outline of German pollutant law. (Helga Lüdtke)
content.title_en: Pollutants in the environment : chemical bases for the assessment of air, water and soil pollution

content.text: Small world : an academic romance. Satirical novel from the world of learned literary professors, which from one congress to another jettisons on the hunt for attention, erotic adventures and scientific fame.
content.title_en: Small world : an academic romance

content.text: The threatened future: are we endangering our fertility and survival?. Klappentext: The horror vision of a human-free earth could become a reality faster than we imagine. The zoologist and pharmacist Theo Colborn and her co-authors provide comprehensive information for the first time on a previously unknown consequence of global pollution: the dramatically decreasing fertility of humans and animals worldwide. An exciting science report, which also seeks solutions.
content.title_en: The threatened future: are we endangering our fertility and survival?

content.text: Global environmental protection as a distribution problem in the North-South conflict : Causes and solutions presented by the example of the grubbing-up of tropical rain forests. Klappentext: After an overview of the different concepts of "Sustainable Development", the author presents the example of the use of tropical forests, which sectors cause environmental damage and which macroeconomic contribution these sectors make. Subsequently, the causes of environmental damage in developing countries are discussed, e.g. sectoral incentives of economic policy, lack of property rights, population growth, poverty and debt. Subsequently, the efficiency and effectiveness of national and international policies are examined with the help of general equilibrium models.
content.title_en: Global environmental protection as a distribution problem in the North-South conflict : Causes and solutions presented by the example of the grubbing-up of tropical rain forests
