content.text: What bits and trees combine: Sustainable design of digitalisation; Bits & trees, the conference for digitalization and sustainability, Technische Universität Berlin in November 2018. The conference »Bits & trees« (2018 in Berlin) has been the largest debate forum for digitalization and sustainability. More than 50 authors from the tech scene, the sustainability movement and development cooperation show in this book of the conference how digitalization can advance social-ecological change. The contributions shed light on the impact of our digital consumption in the global south, the sustainable use of data or the risks and potentials of a digitised economic system. The focus is always on the urgent question: Which digitalization do we want? The various answers to this question make clear: A future-proof digitalisation must be oriented less towards the interests of individual economic actors, but rather towards the common good. Selected contributions from »Bits & trees« numerous infographics and portraits give ideas on how digitalization can make the world better.
content.title_en: What connects bits and trees : Sustainable design of digitalization ; Bits & trees, the conference for digitalization and sustainability, Technische Universität Berlin in November 2018

content.text: Sacred Spaces in Judaism : Festschrift für Salomon Korn. Architektur – Gesellschaft – Religion: These are the coordinates of the Festschrift for the sociologist, architect and chairman of the Frankfurt Jewish Community, Salomon Korn. "Sakrale Raumen im Judik" spans the archetype of the architecture of the temple over temple concepts, virtual sacral spaces, prayer rooms to synagogues from the Middle Ages to classical modernism. The volume gathers contributions to a conference of the same topic from various sub-divisions of the Heidelberg University of Jewish Studies, whose chairman of the board of trustees Salomon Korn was over many years, and includes studies of other researchers on the subject. As a result, he illustrates the surprising breadth of sacred space concepts in Judaism and underlines the Jewish part in the history of European sacred architecture.
content.title_en: Sacred Spaces in Judaism : Festschrift für Salomon Korn

content.text: The contributions of this collection deal with theories and models as well as approaches to the practice of debt prevention and poverty reduction. The authors of contributions investigate how disadvantaged groups of people can be reached, they shed light on the links between poverty, debt and debt prevention and they further explore the communication of financial knowledge and competence for the target group of students and trainees.The book presents the current discourse on the practice of debt prevention in German-speaking countries and gives help to further develop the work on this topic.The content of debt and poverty as the subject of prevention and counselling The theories and concepts of prevention Methodical approaches and innovations Challenges and perspectives of debt prevention The target groups of lecturers and students of education, psychology, sociology and social work Practitioners in social work The editor Dr. Christoph Mattes is a lecturer at the University of Applied Sciences Northwestern Switzerland (FHNWS). content.text: Crisis of the Future II : Responsibility and freedom in the face of apocalyptic scenarios. Current debates of self-conciliation in Western societies are characterized by crisis discourses that often use religious-apocalyptic symbolism. The future, it seems, can, at least in European discourses, often only be thought in the mode of the catastrophy. Such a thinking of the future has an impact on current action and challenges our traditional ethical guiding concepts. Who can take responsibility for the future if the catastrophe seems inevitable?This volume gathers the contributions of the interdisciplinary final conference of the Research College "The Crisis of the Future" of the Centre for Religion, Economics and Politics (ZRWP) Basel. The texts deal ethically with the questions that bring about current forms of future discourse.
content.title_en: Crisis of the Future II : Responsibility and Freedom in the Face of Apocalyptic Scenarios

content.text: Everyday and transition practices in support of young people: Between self-determination, attachment and societal adaptation demands. Help for young people must be designed in such a way that they have a good chance at the end of the day being able to live a self-determined life. What does everyday life in stationary aid institutions look like in order to achieve this goal? How can transitions be measured by different perspectives? What social and legal policy decisions are necessary? In this volume, everyday and transitional practices in different help systems for young people are exposed from different perspectives. Help for young people must be designed in such a way that they can ultimately have a good chance to live independently. How must everyday life look at stationary help institutions so that this goal is achieved? How can transitions be meaningfully shaped by different perspectives? Help for young people must be designed in such a way that they can ultimately have a good chance of self-determined life.
content.title_en: Practices in everyday and transitional situations in support of young people: Between self-determination, attachment and societal adaptation requirements

content.text: Documentation as a pastoral task: electronic patient dossiers in the context of Spiritual Care. In clinical pastoral care, it is increasingly practice that the pastoral care workers document their work digitally, make it interprofessionally accessible and record it for various purposes. But what are the possibilities and limits of such documentation? In the German-speaking area, this topic is being investigated within the framework of a National Fund project and for the first time comprehensively discussed: Basic considerations are complemented by practical-theological, ethical and legal perspectives as well as by those from the concrete medical and nursing practice. Not least, practical-theological questions are addressed: How is the pastoral care secret to be documented in interprofessional terms? What concrete documentation practices are developing? Many questions connected with this complex and new topic, such as data protection, are being discussed in detail.
content.title_en: Documentation as pastoral task : electronic patient dossiers in the context of Spiritual Care

content.text: Artificial Intelligence, Democracy and Privatity. This volume contains selected contributions from the annual conference of the Forum Privatity, 2021. It analyses the current challenges that arise from the development of artificial intelligence (AI) for privacy, informational self-determination, and democracy and how these can be addressed by governance mechanisms. The contributions focus on AI's use for profiling and monitoring, on issues of dissemination and discovery of disinformation by AI, as well as on the use of AI in the health and care sector. This volume contains selected papers from the 2021 annual conference affiliated to ‘Forum Privatity, which analysis the current challenges posed by the development of artificial intelligence (AI) to privacy, informational self-determination and democracy, and how they can be addressed through governance measures. The contributions focus on the use of AI through the identification of the identification of the disease and disease.
content.title_en: Artificial intelligence, democracy and privacy

content.text: Variants of change: the region in recent history 1970-2020. It may be surprising that "big processes" such as globalisation or digitalization have once again brought the region into the focus of historical interest. But here, the social changes "after the boom" were indeed the most evident. Given the transformative quality of these years, research now distinguishes winners and losers, referring to serious regional differences. The authors of the volume take this as an opportunity to examine a number of different regional topics more closely and to elaborate special "variants of change" since 1970. It is evident that acute need for action below the national level was usually recognized early and the social groups and actors on the ground proved to be the real designers of change. However, the regions were always affected to a varying extent due to their respective dispositions and potentials and therefore suggested very specific development paths in many cases.
content.title_en: Variants of change: the region in recent history 1970-2020

content.text: After the Roman Empire, the buildings were used for the trade and money traffic, ranging from storage buildings in important economic centres and port locations to bank and stock exchange buildings in the central squares of the cities. These buildings were often examined by archaeologists and building historians, with the emphasis on design and design. Economic historians were intensively involved in trade and money transactions without having to consider the connection with building matters. Interdisciplinary cooperation opens up new perspectives. With the knowledge of economic processes, buildings can be better understood, and buildings can make visible economic processes. This became clear at the first exchange of ideas between the various research disciplines. The present conference volume contains contributions on trade forms and trade relations, he presents storage buildings and merchant houses and illuminates with the Magdalensberg in Carinthia a significant center of ore extraction and metal processing. The Roman Basilica takes a special place as a great development building of the Roman Empire and a forum of its counter-concepts, the latter of the Roman Empire's new architectural law.
content.title_en: Economic buildings in the ancient city : International Colloquium, 16 - 17 November 2012, Karlsruhe

content.text: Developments in Europe : Consequences for the development of Bavaria. The volume contains eight papers presented at the 17th seminar for regional planners in Bavaria in October 1994, dealing with the current situation of the development of Bavaria (1994) and the global and European economic structural changes. They show the reactions in spatial planning to the new challenges and demonstrate the need, but also the limitations, for coordinated European spatial planning.
content.title_en: Developments in Europe: Consequences for the development of Bavaria

content.text: To be seen: queer lives 1900-1950. The contributions collected in the volume represent the history of queer life plans - from the first emancipation movements around the turn of the century, to attempts at self-empowerment in the Weimar Republic, to the destruction of queer subcultures under the National Socialist regime and the continuing discrimination against LGBTIQ people in the post-war period. Since the late 19th century, more and more people have been confidently advocating the recognition of queer lifestyles. These pioneers formed collectives, gained their hearing and questioned dominant gender categories politically, scientifically and artistically. In the form of essays, interviews and works of art, authors and artists have been investigating this struggle for recognition, which was violently suppressed, destroyed and remembered by the National Socialists with the takeover of power after 1945.
content.title_en: To be seen : queer lives 1900-1950

content.text: Diversity and representation : Affiliation and exclusion in the literary museum and in literary studies. The analysis and teaching of literary texts of the early 19th century has a wide range of potentials for dealing with diversity, belonging and exclusion. The contributors ask how cultural diversity in the museum and literature and educational practice leads to critical reflections and new perspectives on canonized objects. The focus is on the options for the representation of diversity in the literary museum and in literary studies. In addition, they bring together theoretical and practical accesses and develop a new methodological-theoretical diversity.
content.title_en: Diversity and representation : membership and exclusion in the literary museum and in literary studies

content.text: Resilience as a success factor in tourism : Contributions from science and practice to the development of destinations. This is an open access book. Resilience is one of the central topics of the future in tourism today. Under the conditions of persistent crises and rapid change processes, issues of resistance and adaptability have become increasingly central. This innovative volume examines what distinguishes more resilient destinations and tourist actors more precisely and how the necessary transformation of the industry succeeds. In addition to current practical insights from different regions, relevant topics are addressed, such as: - the role of diversity, - resilience in destination management, - the importance of citizen participation, - the consideration of the perceptions of the local population and - resilience in wine and hiking tourism. An exciting source of inspiration for a key topic of the tourism industry, which was created in the context of the "5th Deidesheimer Talks on Tourism Science".
content.title_en: Resilience as a success factor in tourism : Contributions from science and practice to the development of destinations

content.text: The state of implementation of resource protection in Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein, from the state and regional planning to the municipal level, is discussed from a storage and raw material economic and planning point of view. Weaknesses in the raw material analysis as well as in the planning of the respective area identification (pre-primary, precautionary and reserve areas) are shown. The existing instrument of the regional planning is sufficient. However, the awareness of what binding planning requirements are and where discretionary possibilities lie is not sufficiently pronounced. The trustful cooperation of all parties involved in resource protection is necessary to meet both the nature and environmental protection as well as the supply of the economy with the necessary mineral raw materials.
content.title_en: Instruments of regional planning and planning for the conservation of raw materials in the countries of Bremen, Hamburg, Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein

content.text: The new century: European time diagnoses and future designs around 1900. This volume looks at Europe-wide discussions and controversy around 1900. The contributions take into account the international dimension of these debates and focus on those topics that contemporaries already paid special attention to and which were of prominent importance for the history of the 20th century. These included war and peace scenarios, the scientific resonation about a "new person", the perspectives of economics and technology, cultural and artistic locational regulations and future designs, the expectations of a new gender order as well as the development of industrial class society. These topics are examined from different locations: from the perspective of social movements as well as from political classes, scientists or professional groups. "Public opinion" of the turn of the century thus ranges into various actors and discutants. The book reconstructs a fascinating panorama image of European public opinion - a panoramic image in which experiences of the past merge with expectations of the future, in which fears, distortions and expanses are likewise abolished as well as hopes, desires and wishes of the university.
content.title_en: The New Century : European Time Diagnoses and Futures around 1900

content.text: Social exclusion through inclusion: prison and criminal assistance between restriction and resocialization. The combination of a tightening criminal policy and restrictive social policy, as it is currently staged, has a rather integrated character in its interaction with social marginal groups. In connection with increasing poverty, social exclusion has become an important issue in recent years. An increasing number of long-term unemployed, the precarious living conditions of migrants in the metropolises, the increasing poverty among young people, all this points to social situations which are substantiated by the concept of social exclusion. The logic of such social processes: the less competitive, the socially vulnerable, the less vulnerable and the more economically and socially vulnerable, the greater the risk of social exclusion of morally degraded persons or groups. A group that combines several characteristics of this is that of the people who have become ill-off.
content.title_en: Social exclusion by inclusion : prison and help between restriction and resocialization

content.text: From hand-to-hand to high-tech : measure, model, represent ; recording methods in historical building research ; interdisciplinary colloquium from 23 - 26 February 2000. From hand-to-hand to high-tech - in this field of tension the current discussion about methods and procedures of building reception in building research, archaeology and preservation of monuments moves. Latest surveying methods, 3D models or virtual reality offer new opportunities for surveying and presentation of buildings, ruins or entire urban facilities. At the same time, many objects require an intensive study on site, which can not only be realized with the traditional methods of hand-to-hand measurement. - In over 30 contributions, in which the interdisciplinary discussion of a colloquium conducted at the Technical University of Cottbus is summarized, potentials and limits of the different methods are clearly presented.The volume includes 38 contributions of a colloquium in the University of Cottbus. The new technical possibilities of measuring on computer programs, 3-D representations and many other new methods have also been extensively used in the field of archaeological surveying and building drawings as well as in the preservation of monuments. The volume of the practical methods is strongly influenced by the state-to-level analysis.
content.title_en: From manual to high tech : measuring, modelling, representing ; admission procedures in historical building research ; interdisciplinary colloquium of 23-26 February 2000

content.text: Cork: History, Architecture, Design 1750 - 2002; [for the special exhibition "Totally Corked?!" Cork: History, Architecture, Design 1750 - 2002 of the museums of the city of Delmenhorst on the North wool from 16.6. to 15.9.2002]. For centuries the constantly renewing bark of cork oaks has been supplying precious material in the countries around the Mediterranean, for example bottle corks. However, the commercial cradle of cork processing has been located in the north-west of Germany since the mid-18th century, around and in the city of Delmenhorst. Since that time, the so-called "propane down" mainly cork grafts have been shipped to wine dealers all over the world. Cork has been used in an incredible variety in architecture, design and fashion since the 18th century: cork has been used as a high-quality insulation material in house construction since ancient times; also as a floor covering, cork is pure or as a major component of linoleum. Less known is the fact that cork has been used for architectural model construction in Italy and Germany since the 18th century as a modern cork industry.
content.title_en: Cork : History, Architecture, Design 1750 - 2002 ; [for the special exhibition "Totally Corked?!" Cork: History, Architecture, Design 1750 - 2002 of the museums of the city of Delmenhorst on the North wool from 16.6. to 15.9.2002]

content.text: The Colour White: Colour Rausch and Colour Distinction in Architecture; [as catalogue of the exhibition "The Colour White - Colour Rausch and Colour Distinction in Architecture", April 27 - June 22, 2003, Stadthaus Ulm]. content.text: Broadband perspectives: fast access to innovative applications; with 137 illustrations and 7 tables; [Specialized conference "Broadband Perspectives - Fast Access to Innovative Applications" of the Munich district]. Worldwide, the expansion of telecommunications networks to a broadband infrastructure is in full swing. DSL is the backbone of fast Internet access in many countries. TV cables are increasingly also used for fast Internet access. For mobile participants, wireless access technologies provide complementary solutions. DAB and DVB are used for the transmission of content and data; for the cellular systems of the third generation as well as for the wireless LANs, the non-voice services are in the foreground. The questions are: How does broadband pay off? What do business models look like? Who finances the expansion of the infrastructure? The Munich district has carried out a critical inventory of the worldwide efforts. Supported by high-ranking experts, the current developments and the future perspectives were analysed.
content.title_en: Broadband perspectives : fast access to innovative applications ; with 137 illustrations and 7 tables ; [Conference on "Broadband Perspectives - Fast access to innovative applications" by the Munich district]

content.text: Altar Room as a community space : Redesign of existing churches; [a symposium organized at the Catholic-Theological Private University Linz in May 2003]. The transformation of existing churches, especially altar room arrangements, is now the most common undertaking of church construction activities, following the boom of the new buildings from the post-war period to the 1980s. Despite new insights into historical spatial situations and new liturgical theological considerations, the new challenge for the communities, theological basic views and pastoral requirements remains to be adequately transformed into a spatial design. A symposium organized in May 2003 at the Catholic-Theological Private University Linz/Donau brought together experts from the fields of architecture, monument preservation, art, liturgy and pastoral activities.

content.text: Higher Education didactic qualification : strategies and concepts in an international comparison. The high debt didactic qualification is now an international standard. More and more countries, whose main resource is education, rely on the didactic qualification of their teaching staff. The volume describes the international status: current country examples show the far-reaching changes in this area. In Germany, especially study programmes, networks and increasingly modularized programmes of high debt didactic institutions take an important place.

content.text: "Cities for All" - about visionary and feasible urban development: Martin Neuffer and Rudolf Koldewey; Documentation of the symposium on 20 June 2005 in Hanover. In June 2005, the symposium took place to honour the two Upper Town Directors Martin Neuffer and Rudolf Koldewey of the state capital Hanover. Martin Neuffer's visionary ideas and development opportunities ("Cities for All-Design of a Urban Policy" as the programmatic title of one of his books) and the rather sober and pragmatic thinking and action of Rudolf Koldewey represented the mental tension in which the individual contributions of this documentation are located. As a result, the current challenges of urban development and urban development in the context of the major changes in the urban development policy framework from the point of view of municipal politics, urban research, planning administration and administrative modernization become clear.

content.text: Transgenerational transmission of war-affected childhoods: interdisciplinary studies on the sustainability of historical experiences over four generations. Today's historical research looks at the causes of the Second World War and its effects. This perspective is also offered for the research of war childhoods. The eleven authors agree that education is crucially decisive about life chances and the conviction that educational justice is to be achieved. Their research aims to systematically establish the human right to education and to formulate the standards for political implementation in an educational social policy.
content.title_en: Human right to education and its implementation in Germany : Diagnoses - Reflections - Perspectives

content.text: The media of architecture: an exhibition of the A:AI Archive for Architecture and Engineering Art NRW; [21 November to 7 December 2007, Rudolf Chaudoire-Pavillon, Campus Süd, Technical University Dortmund]. Those who listen to architecture think of buildings. But as much as we are surrounded by buildings as we are everyday, buildings that concern us are very rare for us. They are usually taught us in a wide range of ways: through images, models, texts and other ways of representation. As little as the physical existence of buildings can be denied, no building without media can be created, used and understood. This was the subject of an exhibition at the Faculty of Construction at TU Dortmund, which was prepared and organized with students. The range of architectural representation was presented using selected pieces from the holdings of the A:AI Archive for Architecture and Engineering Art NRW. Even if not according to construction projects, but according to media, sketches, plans, perspectives, detailed drawings, static calculations, models, photos, films, texts and publications were presented.

content.text: The "Schlossbau in der zweiten Half des 15. Jahrhunderts in Mitteldeutschland" (Schlossbau in the second half of the 15th century in Mitteldeutschland) was held at Schloss Sachsenburg. Since 2002, studies on the history of the building have been carried out at Schloss Sachsenburg near Frankenberg/Sa. The very important findings obtained have led to the presentation of a symposium on the construction of the castle in the second half of the 15th century in Mitteldeutschland. This also enabled the presentation of the research results achieved in numerous other Middle German castles. This volume presents the contributions of the most renowned scientists researching the topic.

content.text: Regional and Regional Planning in Baden-Württemberg : an interim assessment on the occasion of the 100th session of the Baden-Württemberg LAG; [joint event of the ARL and the Baden-Württemberg Ministry of Economics on 10 July 2008 at the Haus der Wirtschaft Stuttgart]. In 2008 the Baden-Württemberg Regional Labour Association of the Academy of Spatial Research and Planning will hold its 100th session. This volume, published on the occasion of this anniversary, will draw an interim assessment of the development of regional and regional planning in Baden-Württemberg and present the work, development and essential characteristics of the Baden-Württemberg Regional Labour Community.
content.title_en: Regional and Regional Planning in Baden-Württemberg : an interim assessment at the 100th meeting of the LAG Baden-Württemberg; [joint event of the ARL and the Ministry of Economics Baden-Württemberg on 10 July 2008 at the House of Economics Stuttgart]

content.text: Public financial flows and spatial development: [scientific plenary session 2008]. With the topic "Public financial flows and spatial development" the Academy of Spatial Research and Planning (ARL) addresses questions whose far-reaching and lasting political significance is uncontroversial and whose daily appearance is always in the foreground of public interest. Spatial effects are derived from all fiscal policies, including those which do not have an explicit spatial development policy objective. Nevertheless, the spatial implications of financial policy decisions are often not included in the political decision-making processes and spatial consequences of political decisions are not sufficiently analysed and evaluated systematically. In this context, the present volume offers exemplary studies and regionalized analyses as well as theoretical considerations on the spatial effects of public funding and use in a wide range of current economic and financial policy areas. With this publication, the ARL pursues the goal in the intersection between spatial research and financial science to promote scientific and political discourse and to restrict both.
content.title_en: Public financial flows and spatial development : [2008 Scientific Plenary Session]

content.text: Martin Elsaesser and Neue Frankfurt: [in the context of "Phänomen Expressionismus 2009 - 2011 - ein Projekt des Kulturfonds FrankfurtRheinMain" ; on the occasion of the exhibition "Martin Elsaesser und das Neue Frankfurt" (10 October 2009 - 14 March 2010), organized by the German Architecture Museum, Department of Culture and Science, City of Frankfurt am Main]. The accompanying book for the exhibition at the Deutsche Architekturmuseum Frankfurt am Main from 10 October 2009 to 31 January 2010. - - The publication takes on a double role: it accompanies an exhibition and documents in detail the architect's works that remained as project during his time as artistic director of the Hochbauamt in Frankfurt between 1925 and 1932. Moreover, it deepens aspects such as Elsaesser's difficult role as a leading co-designer of the Neue Frankfurt and the economic, political and personal conditions of his term of office. The book also approaches the teacher and (family) person Elsaesser and undertakes excursions in other creative phases of the construction artist, who has left a rich work before and few prominent buildings after the Frankfurt phase. The modernist's approach to the interpretation of his work is widely reheard in 1925.
content.title_en: Martin Elsaesser and the Neue Frankfurt : [in the context of "Phänomen Expressionismus 2009 - 2011 - a project of the Kulturfonds FrankfurtRheinMain" ; on the occasion of the exhibition "Martin Elsaesser and the Neue Frankfurt" (10 October 2009 - 14 March 2010), organized by the German Architecture Museum, Department of Culture and Science, City of Frankfurt am Main]

content.text: Myth Monument : urban strategies in architecture and art since 1945; [goes back to an international conference held in January 2010 at the Kunsthistorisches Institut der Ruhr-Universität Bochum under the title "Mythos Monument. Urban strategies in architecture and art since 1945"]. The reflection of the monumental is a central theme of architecture as well as of art after 1945. On the one hand, this is evidenced by the attempts to renew modern architecture by means of a new understanding of concepts. On the other hand, art has been characterized by the desire to comment on or deconstruct the monumental self-understanding of architecture since the 1960s at the latest. - - The volume shows how architecture and art enter into a complex dialogue in this way, which can be observed on different levels: from the immediate confrontation in urban space through the conception of utopian places and antimonuments to the critical commentary of destroyed or reconstructed buildings and monuments.
content.title_en: Myth Monument : Urban Strategies in Architecture and Art since 1945; [goes back to an international conference held in January 2010 at the Kunstgeschichtliches Institut der Ruhr-Universität Bochum under the title "Mythos Monument. Urban Strategies in Architecture and Art since 1945"]

content.text: B1-A40 - the beauty of the big road: a project in the urban space of the A40 from Duisburg to Dortmund, 12.06.2010 - 08.08.2010 ; Atelier van Lishout; Finger ... ; [on the occasion of the exhibition "B1-A40 The beauty of the big road. A project in the urban space of the A40 from Duisburg to Dortmund"]. Due to its all-day closure in July, the motorway A 40 became probably the largest media event of the European Capital of Culture RUHR.2010. The exhibition "B1-A40 - The beauty of the big road" reflects, as the A 40 in a unique reversal from the periphery to the centre, becoming the central boulevard of the Ruhr metropolis with its over six million inhabitants. Schrebergartenen and shopping miles, cultural production and shadow economy - they all use the "big road" as a platform, node, infrastructure. This situation offers the possibility to examine urgent questions of the "Urban Age" on site: how do spaces generate themselves beyond targeted planning and use interests? And what distinguishes these - for planning and politics largely invisible spaces - are presented by artists, scientists, planning and planaries and new conditions?
content.title_en: B1-A40 - the beauty of the big road : a project in the city area of the A40 from Duisburg to Dortmund, 12.06.2010 - 08.08.2010 ; Atelier van Lishout; Finger ... ; [on the occasion of the exhibition "B1-A40 The beauty of the big road. The topics of land use development and reliable land use monitoring, taking into account the objectives of a sustainable land use policy, are becoming increasingly important for policy, spatial planning and environmental protection in view of the increasing land competition and ambitious land saving targets. Meanwhile, an intensive discussion has begun on how and on which data basis the use of land for settlement and transport can be measured, how qualitative aspects of land use can be included in addition to the official land survey, which role new high-resolution topographic geobase data and building data play in the process of capturing land development potential and how corresponding analysis results can be clearly and comprehensiblely visualized. content.text: Silk in the early and high medieval women's monastery : Possession - Meaning - Re-use ; [Essen's first meeting of the Women's Foundations and the Catholic Academy "The Wolfsburg" from 2 - 4 November 2012]. Valuable silks from Byzantium and Central Asia were exclusive goods, comparable to gold, gems and gems or cameos. In the early and high Middle Ages, precious silks usually only came to the West as gifts and were often given away further due to their value. On this way, the precious goods found their way into the disposal of religious communities also from worldly possessions. On the Mathilden-Otto-Kreuz, Essen's Abbessss Mathilde wears a precious garment. Which material is it about, where does it originate, which message should be conveyed to the viewer with the garment? The ways of such textiles for food let ask for political and cultural relations of the community. A second aspect is the conversion of the precious silks in the Middle Ages.
content.title_en: Silk in the Early and Medieval Women's Penitentiary : Possession - Meaning - Re-use ; [Elfth Conference of the Essen Working Group on the Research of the Women's Pencils and the Catholic Academy "Die Wolfsburg" from 2 - 4 November 2012]

content.text: Social Media - New Masses : [... 2nd Symposium on Media Studies of the German Research Foundation]. Mass meetings and the positive or negative fantasies of mass are sparked by different discourses and practices of social control, communication and community formation. But masses are no longer what they once were. From the substitution of mass media research by algorithmic analysis of mass data on the diagnosis of dispersed public in the age of social media to new mass ideas such as swarms, flashmobs and multitudes: the emergence, functioning and effects of digital masses are now to be re-examined and negotiated. Moreover, the changes of the present are an option to re-understand the cultural and media history writing of the masses themselves. The volume outlines this new field of research and gathers analyses of the difference between new and old masses, of the different media technical conditions and of the political consequences of current mass phenomena.

content.text: Environment and empirical social and economic research: Contributions and discussion reports to a conference of the project group "The Socio-Economic Panel" at the German Institute for Economic Research. Environmental research and environmental protection are not only the subject of natural sciences, but empirical social and economic sciences and have their important place in this problem area. The corresponding empirical research serves primarily two purposes: firstly, the representation (description) of the environmental state and its evaluation by the population and its subgroups. This branch of environmental social research is in the tradition of social reporting. Secondly, social and economic research surveys serve for behavioural analysis, i.e. the investigation of determinants of environmental-relevant behaviour and the perception of the environment and its evaluation. -- In this volume, an overview of environmental-oriented social and economic research is given in the first block. The second block contains essays, which are in the tradition of social reporting, while in the third block studies are presented, the environmental behaviour is examined microanalytically.
content.title_en: Environment and empirical social and economic research : Contributions and discussion reports to a conference of the project group "The Socio-Economic Panel" at the German Institute for Economic Research

content.text: Manifestations in Design : Design - Architecture - Engineering. "The artifacts developed in the design process, as well as the things of our designed world, are still under-represented in public and scientific attention. The volume deals with the epistemological role of the manifestations arising in design, which make intentions, methods and creative processes readable. The contributions about and from design, architecture and engineering represent an interdisciplinary inventory in order to ask for a new cross-disciplinary perspective of design in the field of tension between analog and digital planning and technization processes."
content.title_en: Manifestations in Design : Design - Architecture - Engineering

content.text: The conference was held in Mannheim on 29 and 30 September 2000 and the discussion of the topic of "Scientific Annual Meeting of the Society for Economic and Social Cybernetics" was held in Mannheim on 29 and 30 September 2000. The discussion of cybernetics, system thinking and complexity management was the result of the often inadequate reality-related formal modeling and analysis of the "classical" methods. As the assumptions of the typical operating research methods were and are difficult to reconcile with the real requirements of decision-making support, especially at the level of corporate policy, this required the search for other ways to deal with the characteristics of relevant real problems in a proper manner. The observation of the dynamics and complexity of corporate management leads almost inevitably to the encounter with cybernetics and system research. Attempts to reduce the arising complexity have proved problematic or even unsuitable. Instead, it is important to build up the necessary activity repertoire to be successful within a complex environment, but also to react. Cybernetics and system research - in particular in the expression of system dynamics - to make the basic concepts to make them more difficult and to make the context of the discussion of the topic of complex systems.
content.title_en: Decisions in complex systems : Scientific Annual Meeting of the Society for Economic and Social Cybernetics, September 29 and 30, 2000 in Mannheim

content.text: The developmental perspectives of low-income countries: On the importance of knowledge and institutions. Knowledge and institutions are important development factors for the so-called low-income countries. What exactly is meant by "knowledge" and "institutions" and what political conclusions to draw - these are the central issues which the Developmental Committee of the Social Policy Association addressed at its Annual Meeting 2000. This volume contains the presentations and correspondents held at this meeting. -- It shows that "knowledge" is important on the one hand in terms of education and human capital. On the other hand, however, special knowledge, such as the effects of macropolitics, centralisation or decentralisation, from privatisation, from regulation to knowledge about the consequences of increased use of information and communication technologies, is important. -- "institutions" are important for the development of low-income countries, on the one hand, from the point of view of how economic, political or social processes are to be organized, so that they have as favourable growth and welfare effects as possible. On the other hand, the well-known question plays a role in ensuring that less of qualitative optimism is to the development, and the extent of the institution to be more concretely of knowledge.

content.text: Indeterminate signatures of technology: a new interpretation of the technological world. Not that a fundamental uncertainty has not always been part of life or a more or less constant and universal condition of human existence, appears as a problem, but - that with the experience of an increase in uncertainty a technology connected with society is affected by it and involved in the uncertainty process; - that social freedom and option gains go hand in hand with after-sustaining loss of orientation; - that the technoscientific generation of knowledge brings forth novel zones of non-knowledge; - that we cannot know what we should actually do and - that dealing with this fact is the starting condition for a contemporary-incontinuous philosophy of technology. The contributions of this volume (including Dreyfus, Dupuy, Hörning, Hubig, Nordmann and Willke) are not only based on the different aspects of this development. They also make an attempt to estimate the socio-technical determination and the radical strategies of union (the self-evidentialization) in the new task of a "requiretly determined world.
content.title_en: Indeterminability signatures of technology: a new interpretation of the technological world

content.text: Palatium Sacrum : Sacredness at the Court of the Middle Ages : Places, Things, Rituals. Cross-section of current research on the religious culture of the medieval court. Fundamental studies on a hitherto neglected aspect of pre-modern residence research in a perspective extending beyond Europe. 'The volume combines 17 contributions from an international conference held at the University of Göttingen from 18-20 June 2015. He raises the question of the manifestations and practices of the sacred in pre-modern courts, whether in buildings, objects or rituals. The focus of a cross-cultural discourse is the post-antique palace with its religious places and zones, but also other forms of cultic tabooization and sanctioning, in which the border between "profan" and "sacral" is often difficult to determine. The temporal framework ranges from antiquity to the late Middle Ages, the cultural spectrum from Western Europe and Byzantineism to the Islamic courts in Syria and Al-Andalus.'
content.title_en: Palatium Sacrum : Sacredness at the court of the Middle Ages : Places, things, rituals

Germany, Arrival Country at the German Pavilion at the 15th Architecture Biennale 2016 in Venice. The refugee building atlas expands the considerations about the German arrival cities from the first volume. What role do architects and city planners play in the implementation of sustainable solutions for the accommodation of new arrivals in Germany? Which construction projects can serve as prototypes for affordable housing? Using about 55 construction projects, a look into the future of the German cities is ventured. Photographs by Anja Weber and detailed project presentations, which were created after visits on site, provide insights into the everyday life of German refugee accommodation

content.text: Planetary nebulae: multi-wavelength probes of stellar and galactic evolution : proceedings of the 323rd Symposium of the International Astronomical Union held in Beijing, China, October 10-14, 2016. Planetary nebulae, glowing shells of ionized gas, are the spectacular products of the evolution of low- and intermediate-mass stars. For astrophysicists, they are important laboratories for the understanding of atomic, molecular, dust, and plasma processes in different cosmic environments; they enable the exploration of the fundamental physics of single and binary star evolution including nucleosynthesis, rotation, mass transfer and loss, and magnetic fields; and they help trace stellar populations, the kinematics, and chemistry of galaxies including our own galaxy, the Milky Way. This volume reviews the current status of this vibrant research field in the form of invited reviews, contributed talks, and posters presented at the IAU Symposium 323. It should be of interest to researchers and advanced students interested in this field and in related fields, including stellar physics, the interstellar medium, and Galactic and extragalactic astronomy -- Publisher description

content.text: Faking, forging, counterfeiting : discredited practices at the margins of mimesis. Forgeries are an omnipresent part of our culture and closely related to traditional ideas of authenticity, legality, authorship, creativity, and innovation. Based on the concept of mimesis, this volume illustrates how forgeries must be understood as autonomous aesthetic practices - creative acts in themselves - rather than as mere rip-offs of an original work of art. The proceedings bring together research from different scholarly fields. They focus on various mimetic practices such as pseudo-translations, imposters, identity theft, and hoaxes in different artistic and historic contexts. By opening up the scope of the aesthetic implications of fakes, this anthology aims to consolidate forging as an autonomous method of creation.
content.title_en: Faking, forging, counterfeiting : discredited practices at the margins of mimesis

It is devoted to the publication of basic and applied studies broadly related to this area. The chapters present the development of numerical methods, computational techniques, and case studies in the energy applications. Also, they offer the fundamental knowledge for using CFD in energy applications through new technical approaches. Besides, they describe the CFD process steps and provide benefits and issues for using CFD analysis in understanding the flow complicated phenomena and its use in the design process. Zied DrissDr. Driss is Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at National School of Engineers of Sfax (ENIS). He received his Engineering Diploma in 2001, his Master Degree in 2003, his PhD in 2008 and his HDR in 2013 in Mechanical Engineering from ENIS at University of Sfax, Tunisia. He is interested on the development of numerical and experimental techniques for solving problems in mechanical engineering and energy applications. Also, his research has been focused on the interaction between Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Computational Structure Dynamics (CSD) codes. As a result of his research, he is principal or co-principal investigator on more than 80 papers in peer-reviewed journals, more than 150 communications to international conferences, 10 books and 40 books chapters. Also, he is the main inventors of 2 patents. Currently, Dr. Driss is a Chief of Project in the Laboratory of Electromechanical Systems (LASEM), an Editorial in Chief for two international journals, an Editorial Board Member and reviewer for different international journals, an Editor for different books, a General Chair of two bi-annual international conferences and an active member in different national and international associations. Prof. Dr. Brahim Necib Dr. B.Necib is a Professor and Head of Research in Mechanical Engineering Department, Laboratory of mechanics at the University of Mentouri Constantine, Algeria. He received his Philosophy Doctor (Ph. D) and his Master in Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering at Purdue University W. Lafayette Indiana, USA in 1987 and 1982 respectively. He got his Engineer degree in Mechanical Engineering from the National Polytechnic School of Algiers, Algeria in 1980. His work interest is on the development of numerical and experimental techniques for solving practical problems in mechanical and aeronautical engineering. His research work is focused on the aerodynamics, aero elasticity, propulsion and the analysis of static and dynamic discrete and continuum structures as well as the composite and the new smart materials using the finite elements numerical methods. As a result of his research work he is the main supervisor of 10 doctors of state, 30 magiters in mechanical engineering, 10 masters of sciences, 25 engineers of state in mechanics and the principal responsible of 11 national projects of research (CNEPRU). He is the principal authors and co-authors in 20 international and national papers in indexed journals and more than 150 international communications. Also, he is the editor of 02 published bloc notes on «Continuum Mechanics» and «Finite Element Methods». Prof. Necib was the head of the Research Laboratory of Mechanics up to 2008. Actually he is the responsible of research team of 'aerodynamics, complex structures and news materials' and he is an active member in many national research commissions and scientific associations.Prof. Dr. Hao-Chun ZhangDr. Hao-Chun Zhang is currently a Professor in School of Energy Science and Engineering, Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT). He is the deputy head of the Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering, head of Institute of Nuclear Reactor Engineering, HIT, and executive professor of HIT-CORYS Nuclear System Simulation International Joint Research Center(Sino-France). With BSC (Engineering) in 1999, MSC (Engineering) in 2001 and Ph.D. in 2007 from Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT), Dr. Zhang joined HIT in September 2004. Dr. Zhang has about 150 research publications in peer-reviewed journals and conferences, 2 books, and 2 translations of foreign books. Apart from the main research in the area of engineering thermo-physics, currently his research covers computational energy science, nuclear system simulation, and ultrasonic aircraft thermal protection. Dr. Zhang is a recipient of the research fellowship of the Krupp Foundation and DAAD, Germany. He is the reviewer of more than 20 journals, many conferences and scientific funds in the area of nuclear engineering, heat transfer, mechanics and sustainable energy. Dr. Zhang is now in charge of research projects from DFG, national research natural foundation of China, ministry of education of China, ministry of science and technology of China and funds from international and enterprises collaboration. Dr. Zhang is the member of AAAS, ASME and AIAA, Director of China Energy Research Society. He was awarded the 2016 Best Paper of ASME MNHMT, 2015 Most Valued Reviewer by Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer, 2012 DAAD/DFG funds for Chinese scholar, the 2011 outstanding reviewer by ASME Journal of Heat Transfer and 2008 Krupp Fellowship for Chinese Young Scholar from Germany.

content.text: Advances in intelligent analysis of medical data and decision support systems. This volume is a result of the fruitful and vivid discussions during the MedDecSup'2012 International Workshop bringing together a relevant body of knowledge, and new developments in the increasingly important field of medical informatics. This carefully edited book presents new ideas aimed at the development of intelligent processing of various kinds of medical information and the perfection of the contemporary computer systems for medical decision support. The book presents advances of the medical information systems for intelligent archiving, processing, analysis and search-by-content which will improve the quality of the medical services for every patient and of the global healthcare system. The book combines in a synergistic way theoretical developments with the practicability of the approaches developed and presents the last developments and achievements in medical informatics to a broad range of readers: engineers, mathematicians, physicians, and PhD students.--

content.text: Combinatorial methods in topology and algebra. Combinatorics plays a prominent role in contemporary mathematics, due to the vibrant development it has experienced in the last two decades and its many interactions with other subjects. This book arises from the INdAM conference "CoMeTA 2013 - Combinatorial Methods in Topology and Algebra,'' which was held in Cortona in September 2013. The event brought together emerging and leading researchers at the crossroads of Combinatorics, Topology and Algebra, with a particular focus on new trends in subjects such as: hyperplane arrangements; discrete geometry and combinatorial topology; polytope theory and triangulations of manifolds; combinatorial algebraic geometry and commutative algebra; algebraic combinatorics; and combinatorial representation theory. The book is divided into two parts. The first expands on the topics discussed at the conference by providing additional background and explanations, while the second presents original contributions on new trends in the topics addressed by the conference
content.title_en: Combinatorial methods in topology and algebra

content.text: The democratization of artificial intelligence : net politics in the era of learning algorithms. "After a long time of neglect, Artificial Intelligence is once again at the center of most of our political, economic, and socio-cultural debates. Recent advances in the field of Artificial Neural Networks have led to a renaissance of dystopian and utopian speculations on an AI-rendered future. Algorithmic technologies are deployed for identifying potential terrorists through vast surveillance networks, for producing sentencing guidelines and recidivism risk profiles in criminal justice systems, for demographic and psychographic targeting of bodies for advertising or propaganda, and more generally for automating the analysis of language, text, and images. Against this background, the aim of this book is to discuss the heterogenous conditions, implications, and effects of modern AI and Internet technologies in terms of their political-dimension: What does it mean to critically investigate efforts of net politics in the age of machine learning algorithms?"--Back cover
content.title_en: The democratization of artificial intelligence : net politics in the era of learning algorithms

content.text: Networked Embedded Sensing and Control : Workshop NESC'05: University of Notre Dame, USA, October 2005 Proceedings. Recent technological developments in sensing, communications, control and computation have created an emerging class of complex systems hereon called networked embedded systems. These systems can be roughly described as collections of spatially distributed sensors, actuators and controllers whose behaviour is coordinated through wired or wireless communication links. This integration between different technologies and scientific domains presents new and challenging fundamental problems underlying the theoretical foundations for this class of systems. This workshop aims at bringing together researchers working of different aspects of networked embedded systems in order to exchange research experiences and to identify the main scientific challenges in this exciting new area. This volume of Springer’s Lecture Notes in Computer Science series records th the proceedings of the 8 International Workshop on Digital Mammography (IWDM), which was held in Manchester, UK, June 18–21, 2006. The meetings bringtogetheradiversesetofresearchers(physicists,mathematicians,computer scientists, engineers), clinicians (radiologists, surgeons) and representatives of industry, who are jointly committed to developing technology, not just for its ownsake,but to supportclinicians inthe earlydetection andsubsequentpatient management of breast cancer. The conference series was initiated at a 1993 meeting of the SPIE in San Jose, with subsequent meetings hosted every two years by researchers around the world. Previous meetings were held in York, Chicago, Nijmegen, Toronto, Bremen, and North Carolina. It is interesting to re?ect on the changes that have occurred during the past 13 years. Then, the dominant technology was ?lm-screen mammography; now it is full-?eld digital mammography. Then, there were few screening programmes world-wide; now there are many. Then, there was the hope that computer-aided detection (CAD) of early signs of cancer might be possible; now CAD is not only a reality but (more importantly) a commercially led clinical reality. Then, algorithmswerealmostentirelyheuristicwithlittleclinicalsupport;nowthereis arequirementforsubstantialclinicalsupportforanyalgorithmthatisdeveloped and published. However, upon re?ection, could we have predicted with absolute certainty what would be the key questions to be addressed over the subsequent (say) six years? No! That is the nature, joy, and frustration of research. There are more blind alleys to explore than there are rich veins that bring gold (in all senses of that analogy!).

This volume contains the proceeding of the 5th International Conference on - age and Video Retrieval (CIVR), July 13–15, 2006, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ, USA: http://www. civr2006. org. Image and video retrieval cont- ues to be one of the most exciting and fast-growing research areas in the ?eld of multimedia technology. However, opportunities for exchanging ideas between researchers and users of image and video retrieval systems are still limited. The InternationalConferenceonImageandVideo Retrieval(CIVR)hastakenonthe mission of bringing together these communities to allow researchers and prac- tioners around the world to share points of view on image and video retrieval. A uniquefeatureoftheconferenceistheemphasisonparticipationfrompractiti- ers. The objective is to illuminate critical issues and energize both communities for the continuing exploration of novel directions for image and video retrieval. We receivedover 90 submissions for the conference. Eachpaper wascarefully reviewed by three members of the program committee, and then checked by one of the program chairs and/or general chairs. The program committee consisted of more than 40 experts in image and video retrieval from Europe, Asia and North America, and we drew upon approximately 300 high-quality reviews to ensure a thorough and fair review process. The paper submission and review process was fully electronic, using the EDAS system. The quality of the submitted papers was very high, forcing the committee members to make some di?cult decisions. Due to time and space constraints, we could only accept 18 oral papers and 30 poster papers. We welcome you to the 7th International Conference on E-commerce and Web Technologies (EC-Web 2006) held in Krakow, Poland, in conjunction with DEXA 2006. This conference was organized for the first time in Greenwich, UK, in 2000, and it has been able to attract an increasing number of participants and interest, reflecting the progress made in the field. As in the previous years, EC-Web 2006 served as a forum bringing together researchers from academia and practitioners from industry to discuss the current state of the art in e-commerce and Web technologies. Inspiration and new ideas emerged from intensive discussions that took place during the keynote address, the formal sessions and the social events. The conference attracted 88 paper submissions and each paper was reviewed by three Program Committee members. The Program Committee selected 24 papers for presentation and publication (an acceptance and publication rate of 27%). We have to confess that this task was not that easy due to the high quality of the submitted papers. We would like to express our thanks to our colleagues who helped put together the technical program: the Program Committee members and external reviewers for their timely and rigorous reviews of the papers, and the Organizing Committee for their help in the administrative work and support. We owe special thanks to Gabriela Wagner for her helping hand concerning the administrative and organizational tasks of this conference. content.text: Stability and ductility of steel structures. Chapter headings: Foreword. Preface. State-of-the-Art. Beams and Beam-Columns. Steel and Composite Frames. Plates and Plated Structures. Shells. Connections. Bridge and Bridge Piers. Evaluation and Retrofit of Damaged Structures. Low Cycle Fatigue and Fracture. Author index. Keyword index The near-field earthquake which struck the Hanshin-Awaji area of Japan before dawn on January 17, 1995, in addition to snatching away the lives of more than 6,000 people, inflicted horrendous damage on the region's infrastructure, including the transportation, communication and lifeline supply network and, of course, on buildings, too. A year earlier, the San Fernando Valley area of California had been hit by another near-field quake, the Northridge Earthquake, which dealt a similarly destructive blow to local infrastructures. Following these two disasters, structural engineers and researchers around the world have been working vigorously to develop methods of design for the kind of structure that is capable of withstanding not only the far-field tectonic earthquakes planned for hitherto, but also the full impact of near-field earthquake. Of the observed types of earthquake damage to steel structures, there are some whose causes are well understood, but many others continue to present us with unresolved problems. To overcome these, it is now urgently necessary for specialists to come together and exchange information. The contents of this volume are selected from the Nagoya Colloquium proceedings will become an important part of the world literature on structural stability and ductility, and will prove a driving force in the development of future stability and ductility related research and design
content.title_en: Stability and ductility of steel structures

content.text: Early Nutrition and its Later Consequences: New Opportunities : Perinatal Programming of Adult Health — EC Supported Research. Health problems such as hypertension, tendency to diabetes, obesity, blood lipids, vascular disease, bone health, behaviour and learning and longevity may be 'imprinted' during early life. This process is defined as 'programming' whereby a nutritional stimulus operating at a critical, sensitive period of pre and postnatal life imprints permanent effects on the structure, physiology and metabolism. For this reason, academics and industry set-up the EC supported Scientific Workshop -Early Nutrition and its Later Consequences: New Opportunities. The prime objective of the Workshop was to generate a sound exchange of the latest scientific developments within the field of early nutrition to look for opportunities for new preventive health concepts. Further, a closer look was taken at the development of food applications which could provide (future) mothers and infants with improved nutrition that will ultimately lead to better future health. The Workshop was organised by the Dept. of Pediatrics, University of Munich, Germany in collaboration with the Danone Institutes and the Infant Nutrition Cluster, a collaboration of three large research projects funded by the EU.
content.title_en: Early Nutrition and its Later Consequences: New Opportunities : Perinatal Programming of Adult Health — EC Supported Research

content.text: Sensor Systems and Software : First International ICST Conference, S-CUBE 2009, Pisa, Italy, September 7-9, 2009, Revised Selected Papers. This book constitutes the proceedings of the First International ICST Conference, S-CUBE 2009, held in Pisa, Italy, in september 2009. The 16 contributions published in this volume were carefully selected from 45 submitted works in a rigorous peer-reviewed process. In addition to this 3 distinguished researchers were asked to contribute 3 invited papers. The papers examine research challenges facing system development and software support for wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Currently, wireless sensor networks introduce innovative and interesting application scenarios that may support a large amount of different applications including environmental monitoring, disaster prevention, building automation, object tracking, nuclear reactor control, fire detection, agriculture, healthcare, and traffic monitoring. The widespread acceptance of these new services can be improved by the definition of frameworks and architectures that have the potential to radically simplify software development for wireless sensor network based applications. The aim of these new architectures is to support flexible, scalable programming of applications based on adaptive middleware. As a consequence, WSNs require novel programming paradigms and technologies. Moreover the design of new complex systems, characterized by the interaction of different and heterogeneous resources, will allow the development of innovative applications that meet high performance goals. Hence, WSNs require contributions from many fields such as embedded systems, distributed systems, data management, system security and applications.

content.text: Studying Kinetics with Neutrons : Prospects for Time-Resolved Neutron Scattering. Neutrons are extremely versatile probes for investigating structure and dynamics in condensed matter. Due to their large penetration depth, they are ideal for in-situ measurements of samples situated in sophisticated and advanced environments. The advent of new high-intensity neutron sources and instruments, as well as the development of new real-time techniques, allows the tracking of transformation processes in condensed matter on a microscopic scale. The present volume provides a review of the state of the art of this new and exciting field of kinetics with neutrons.
content.title_en: Studying Kinetics with Neutrons : Prospects for Time-Resolved Neutron Scattering

content.text: Performance Engineering : State of the Art and Current Trends. Initially, computer systems performance analyses were carried out primarily because of limited resources. Due to ever increasing functional complexity of computational systems and user requirements, performance engineering continues to play a major role in software development. This book assesses the state of the art in performance engineering. Besides revised chapters drawn from two workshops on performance engineering held in 2000, additional chapters were solicited in order to provide complete coverage of all relevant aspects. The first part is devoted to the relation between software engineering and performance engineering; the second part focuses on the use of models, measures, and tools; finally, case studies with regard to concrete technologies are presented. Researchers, professional software engineers, and advanced students interested in performance analysis will find this book an indispensable source of information and reference
content.title_en: Performance Engineering : State of the Art and Current Trends

content.text: Information Security : 5th International Conference, ISC 2002 Sao Paulo, Brazil, September 30 – October 2, 2002 Proceedings. As distinct from other security and cryptography conferences, the Information Security Conference (ISC) 2002 brought together individuals involved in a wide variety of different disciplines of information security to foster the exchange of ideas. The conference is an outgrowth of the Information Security Workshop, first held in Ishikawa, Japan 1997. ISC 2002 was held in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on September 30– October 2, 2002. The Program Committee considered 81 submissions of which 38 papers were accepted for presentation. These proceedings contain revised versions of the accepted papers. The papers provide a representative sample of both the variety and the truly international scope of information security research conducted currently. The topics addressed range from e-commerce protocols to access control and trust management, and to cryptography and cryptographic algorithms. Many people deserve our gratitude for their contribution to the success of the conference. We would like to thank the General Chair, Routo Terada, for overseeing the local arrangements, including registration and maintaining the conference website, and for the smooth running of the conference. We are grateful to Robbie Ye for his expert help in processing the electronic submissions, reviews and acceptance notifications. Robbie’s enthusiasm and energy greatly simplified the Program Committee’s task of conducting the on-line evaluation of the submitted papers under tight time constraints. Trends in Nanophysics contains reviews on various domains of nanotechnology such as: radiation-induced polymerization, cross-linking and grafting, Mossbauer study of nanomaterials, biomedical applications of nanomaterials, organic thin films for photovoltaics, growth and characterization of semiconductor nanowires, graphene and carbon nanotubes, fractional statistics in nanophysics, nanomechanical properties of materials, ab-initio simulations in nanoscience, fabrication and characterization of ordered atomic-scale structures, plasmonics, and nano-optical studies of motile structures of neuronal cells. Many new tests of gravity and, in particular, of Einstein's general relativity theory will be carried out in the near future: The Lense--Thirring effect and the equivalence principle will be tested in space; moreover, gravitational waves will be detected, and new atomic interferometers and clocks will be built for measurements in gravitational and inertial fields. Both experimental developments and the theoretical concepts are collected in this volume. Exhaustive reviews give an overall insight into the subject of experimental gravitation.

content.text: Ruthenate and Rutheno-Cuprate Materials : Unconventional Superconductivity, Magnetism and Quantum Phase Transitions. Ruthenate materials have come into focus recently because of their very interesting magnetic and superconducting properties. From the first international conference on this topic, the present volume has emerged as a first coherent account of the considerable body of work, both theoretical and experimental, gathered in this field within a short time span. The book has been written in the form of a set of lectures and tutorial reviews with the aim of providing the research community with both a comprehensive and modern source of reference and a tutorial introduction for postgraduate students and nonspecialists working in related areas

content.text: The Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Maps. Quantum maps are presented with special emphasis on their physical origin. They represent a testing ground for understanding concepts in quantized chaotic systems. The book develops and teaches the modern mathematical methods from analytic and algebraic number theory as applied to quantum maps. It gives a broad and in-depth overview of the mathematical problems arising in this area. Also treated are the numerical aspects in quantum chaos such as eigenvalue and eigenfunctions computations for chaotic quantum systems. The book addresses scientists and advanced students in mathematics and mathematical physics
content.title_en: The Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Maps

content.text: The Hydrogen Atom : Precision Physics of Simple Atomic Systems. For more than a century, studies of atomic hydrogen have been a rich source of scientific discoveries. These began with the Balmer series in 1885 and the early quantum theo- ries of the atom, and later included the development of QED and the first successful gauge field theory. Today, hydrogen and its relatives continue to provide new fundamental information, as witnessed by the contributions to this book. The printed volume contains invited reviews on the spectroscopy of hydrogen, muonium, positronium, few-electron ions and frequency metrology and the determination of fundamental constants. The accompanying CD contains, in addition to these reviews, a further 40 contributed papers also presented at the conference "Hydrogen Atom 2" held in summer 2000. Finally, to facilitate a historical comparison, the CD also contains the proceedings of the first "Hydrogen Atom" conference of 1988. The book includes a foreword by Norman F. content.text: Impacts in Mechanical Systems : Analysis and Modelling. This volume constitutes an advanced introduction to the field of analysis, modeling and numerical simulation of rigid body mechanical systems with unilateral constraints. The topics include Moreau's sweeping process, the numerical analysis of nonsmooth multibody systems with friction, the study of energetical restitution coefficients for elasto-plastic models, the study of stability and bifurcation in systems with impacts, and the development of a multiple impact rule for Newton's cradle and the simple rocking model. Combining pedagogical aspects with innovative approaches, this book will not only be of interest to researchers working actively in the field, but also to graduate students wishing to get acquainted with this field of research through lectures written at a level also accessible to nonspecialists
content.title_en: Impacts in Mechanical Systems : Analysis and Modelling

content.text: Distributed Video Sensor Networks. Large-scale video networks are of increasing importance in a wide range of applications. However, the development of automated techniques for aggregating and interpreting information from multiple video streams in real-life scenarios is a challenging area of research. Collecting the work of leading researchers from a broad range of disciplines, this timely text/reference offers an in-depth survey of the state of the art in distributed camera networks. The book addresses a broad spectrum of critical issues in this highly interdisciplinary field: current challenges and future directions, video processing and video understanding, simulation, graphics, cognition and video networks, wireless video sensor networks, communications and control, embedded cameras and real-time video analysis, applications of distributed video networks, and educational opportunities and curriculum-development. Topics and features: Presents an overview of research in areas of motion analysis, invariants, multiple cameras for detection, object tracking and recognition, and activities in video networks Provides real-world applications of distributed video networks, including force protection, wide area activities, port security, and recognition in night-time environments Describes the challenges in graphics and simulation, covering virtual vision, network security, human activities, cognitive architecture, and displays Examines issues of multimedia networks, registration, control of cameras (in simulations and real networks), localization and bounds on tracking Discusses system aspects of video networks, with chapters on providing testbed environments, data collection on activities, new integrated sensors for airborne sensors, face recognition, and building sentient spaces Investigates educational opportunities and curriculum development from the perspective of computer science and electrical engineering This unique text will be of great interest to researchers and graduate students of computer vision and pattern recognition, computer graphics and simulation, image processing and embedded systems, and communications, networks and controls. The large number of example applications will also appeal to application engineers.
content.title_en: Distributed Video Sensor Networks

The systematic study of the physical world is largely based on the design of mathematical models using many different types of ordinary differential, partial differential, integral, and integro-differential equations. The solutions of these equations are therefore of great interest to practitioners and to science in general. With a wealth of cutting-edge research in the field, Integral Methods in Science and Engineering: Computational and Analytic Aspects provides a vivid picture of both the development of theoretical integral techniques and their use in specific science and engineering problems. The volume is an outgrowth of talks presented by world-renowned researchers at the Eleventh International Conference on Integral Methods in Science and Engineering held in Brighton, UK, July 12–14, 2010. The array of topics they address is immense, ranging from theoretical advances in boundary integral methods to applications of analytic and numerical quadrature techniques as diverse as integral equations, finite and boundary elements, conservation laws, hybrid approaches, and more. With ample coverage of theory and applications, this book will be a valuable resource for researchers in applied mathematics, physics, and mechanical and electrical engineering, for graduate students in these disciplines, and for various other professionals who use integration as an essential technique in their work.

Biomarker discovery is an important area of biomedical research that can lead to significant breakthroughs in disease analysis and targeted therapy. Moreover, the discovery and management of new biomarkers is a challenging and attractive problem in the emerging field of biomedical informatics. This volume is a collection of state-of-the-art research from select participants of the “International Conference on Biomedical Data and Knowledge Mining: Towards Biomarker Discovery,” held July 7-9, 2010 in Chania, Greece. content.text: Control of Partial Differential Equations : Cetraro, Italy 2010, Editors: Piermarco Cannarsa, Jean-Michel Coron. The term “control theory” refers to the body of results - theoretical, numerical and algorithmic - which have been developed to influence the evolution of the state of a given system in order to meet a prescribed performance criterion. Systems of interest to control theory may be of very different natures. This monograph is concerned with models that can be described by partial differential equations of evolution. It contains five major contributions and is connected to the CIME Course on Control of Partial Differential Equations that took place in Cetraro (CS, Italy), July 19 - 23, 2010. Specifically, it covers the stabilization of evolution equations, control of the Liouville equation, control in fluid mechanics, control and numerics for the wave equation, and Carleman estimates for elliptic and parabolic equations with application to control. We are confident this work will provide an authoritative reference work for all scientists who are interested in this field, representing at the same time a friendly introduction to, and an updated account of, some of the most active trends in current research. 1 On some recent advances on stabilization for hyperbolic equations -- 2 Notes on the Control of the Liouville Equation -- 3 Some questions of control in ﬂuid mechanics -- 4 Carleman estimates and some applications to control theory -- 5 The Wave Equation: Control and Numerics.
