content.text: The role of microRNA-155 in innate immunity and immunopathology. Summary: In the last 10 years microRNA (miR) research has "exploded" and is now part of general education. Much effort has been made to investigate the biogenesis of these short RNAs. However, it is only little known about their physiological role. MicroRNA-155 (miR-155) is an inducible microRNA, which plays an important role in the regulation of the immune system. It has been shown that miR-155 deficiency leads to a malfunction of the adaptive immune system. These mice cannot establish memory cells as a result of infection. However, it is only little known about the role of miR-155 in the innate immune system. It has been shown that expression of miR-155 positively correlates with the inflammatory status of myeloid cells. In short, if the cellular inflammatory markers are highly regulated, the expression of miR-155 is also highly regulated.

content.text: Social policy between tradition and modernity: state regulations in the intersection of labour market integration and reproduction in Germany, France and Spain. The study asks about the explanatory power of traditions for the divergence of employment-related social policies. Based on a historical analysis of developments and traditional lines, it is shown by the example of Germany, France and Spain that different cultural traditions have developed here, which lead to a specific understanding. Based on the concept of secondary care arrangements, which is elaborated in the historical analysis, a categorization of contemporary regulations is carried out. In this process a theory of different modernization strategies is developed, which creates a basis for further research and, in particular, has a explanatory power for the diversity of regulations beyond the countries analysed; it thus provides an approach point to a culturally sensitive understanding in the field of social policy studies.

content.text: Last-time consumer load management between the energy market and Smart Grid. The system change from conventional demand-oriented generation to supply-based consumption raises the question of a participation of private consumers, which played a decisive role in 2011 with a total share of 26% of the demand for electrical energy in Germany. The present paper examines the flexibility of the load of "private last-consumers" by means of variable tariffing and their application as a method in the Smart Grid system. In view of the state of research on technical and economic background, the question of integrating private last-consumers into grid operation is answered. To this end, flexible tariffs as well as smart metering are explained as prerequisites, as well as the grid development index (GDI) as a classification of the development stage of a smart grid are introduced. In a field trial, the theoretical findings are applied to a distribution network of a suburban small town in Germany. Based on the available real measurement data, it is then examined whether Demand Side Management, which relies on variable tariffs, meets the requirements of a smart grid in suburban and rural areas.
content.title_en: Last-time private consumer load management between energy market and smart grid

content.text: Planning and optimization of flow assembly systems: a contribution taking into account changing requirements for process reliability, product quality and flexibility. Originally, the design of assembly systems in the form of flow systems aimed at an evenly high number of parts of a single product with a high degree of automation. For reasons such as increasing requirements due to customer requests or sales changes, assembly processes are constantly adapted to the changed framework conditions. Such requirements have an impact on the structure and design of flow assembly systems. Thus, aspects such as redundancy, buffering and the integration of quality stations gain in importance when planning such systems. New methods are developed to improve the configuration and operation of post-processing loops, the converging or diverging and parallel structures. The developed structures have more advantages in terms of flexibility, redundancy, availability, utilization and buffer capacities compared to conventional structures.
content.title_en: Planning and optimization of flow assembly systems: a contribution taking into account changing requirements for process reliability, product quality and flexibility

content.text: The Europeanization of North Rhine-Westphalia's energy and climate policy: the reign of CDU/FDP from 2005 to 2010. Can the theses often represented in the political science discussion confirm the loss of significance of the German countries by European integration and the deparliamentaryization of subnational politics? The Europeanization of North Rhine-Westphalia's energy and climate policy did not lead to the exclusion of the country in the European multi-level system and not to the deparliamentarization of subnational politics during the 14th election period. content.text: The city at the gates: Lüneburg and its surroundings in the late Middle Ages. The medieval city did not end at its walls. In many respects, the medieval city space extended beyond its internal area and structured the supposedly empty field beyond the narrower border. These included forests, gardens and other land in bourgeois and communal property, commercial enterprises (goats, mills, quarries) and utilities (wells) as well as military fortifications (land defences). Urban rights of rule in the surrounding countryside were also the focus of the council's policy as were the trade routes necessary for the economic success of a city and its merchants. Niels Petersen reconstructs in detail the surrounding area of the Hanse and salt town of Lüneburg, which in the 15th century belonged to the largest cities in Northern Germany, and orders the results into the city-remote research and the recent "space" discussions. Here it becomes clear that the city space - also in Lüneburg - is not abstractly definable, but rather was practically and symbolically produced by the German Research Forum of Lüneburger Ausgebrüchsches.
content.title_en: The city at the gates : Lüneburg and its surroundings in the late Middle Ages

content.text: The development of a CAE tool for designing flight control and hydraulic systems. The practical support of the engineer in designing flight control and hydraulic systems - including the computer - is the focus of this work. The data is derived from the data that was established during the aircraft design for a new aircraft project. From this the requirements for the flight control system are derived: What moment is necessary to move the control surfaces of the aircraft in all flight situations? At what speed must the control surfaces be ejected. What influence does the required reliability have on the design? With the help of these preliminary considerations the hydraulic, linear actuators of the flight control can then be dimensioned and integrated into the wings or the control systems. Furthermore, the connection of the actuators to the energy systems and computers of the aircraft will be examined. With the help of a stationary calculation the hydraulic system is designed. Finally, it is shown how the design of the aircraft systems can be economically evaluated based on the "Direct Operating Costs".
content.title_en: Development of CAE tool for designing flight control and hydraulic systems

content.text: The use of adaptive learning methods to regulate industrial combustion processes is actively discussed. Learningable models are in principle able to ensure better process management. Likewise, the problems of standard learning methods with the data of real processes are shown. In the main part of the work three improvement approaches are developed: The influence of intoxicated data on the learning process. In order to obtain good models despite such data, both intoxicated points (outliers) are used from the data set as well as robust training methods. The adaptation of a learningable model to changes of the process over long periods of time. It is shown that adapting the data of a process already leads to advantages over a static model. On combustion data the best results are achieved with the weighted combination of adaptive models in ensembles. content.text: Environmental information for consumers: basics, methods and opportunities for impact. Increasing environmental problems are the burden that the past has put on the new millennium. It remains questionable what ecological role the consumer should play and what means can be used to promote environmentally friendly consumer behaviour. Economical foundations about the costs and benefits of ecological action on the one hand, social psychological interdependencies and psychology of consumer behaviour on the other hand form the scientific poles of the present study. Effective behavioural corrections are linked to the convictions of the individual consumer regarding the results of his actions, the expectations of other and the individual barriers to master. The empirical results show where the promising priorities of environmental consumer information lie. It is about information oriented to the consumer needs, which answers in detail in quick access application-related questions, positively achieved instead of failures and dispenses with general moralisation. This information calls for consumers not only from the state and from consumer and environmental associations, but also emphatically from companies.
content.title_en: Environmental information for consumers: basics, methods and opportunities for impact

content.text: The forecasting of the interest rate is traditionally very important in the context of the individual and macroeconomic relevance of interest rate changes. Nevertheless, the scientific literature shows only a relatively few studies which analyse the prognosis quality of econometric methods "out of sample". In the context of a theoretical analysis as well as a broad empirical study, the author shows possibilities of forecasting money and capital market interest rates. In the framework of the strategy underlying the concept of the work "market-based interest rate forecasts" the interest rate development is predicted by market expectations, which are reflected in interest rates and the interest rate structure, are extracted and analysed using econometric methods. The methodical approach of the work is based on recent international studies, in which interest rates and interest rate structure are modelled as so-called regime switching processes. -- In the first main part of the work, the author leads from the perspective of the application-oriented time series analysts into the regime switching technique. In the second main part, the forecasting of the interest rate variables is shown in the context of the theoretical forecasting.
content.title_en: Market-based interest rate forecasts with regime switching models

content.text: The first investment decision must take account of the possibility of making subsequent decisions. Real investment is linked to a variety of different decisions. These decisions depend to a large extent on each other. The initial investment decision must take account of the possibility of making subsequent decisions. This fact becomes particularly relevant when deposits from investment projects are expected in the distant future, i.e. when there is a long time between the initial investment decision and the sale of products. In this case, uncertainty about prices, demand or behaviour of competitors and the possibility of responding to them play an important role. The author deals with the sequential nature of investment decisions under uncertainty. In this respect, models are developed that are based on option price and play-heoretical findings and thus can include both uncertainty about prices and demand as well as the behaviour of competitors in the analysis. From these models, numerous insights that are of considerable importance for the further development of investment theory can be derived.
content.title_en: Sequential investment decisions under uncertainty

content.text: The public is not asked to consider the motives of the public-sector investor, but rather the motives of the public-sector investor, although a closer examination of the motives of the public-sector investor would be of great importance for individual investment decisions. In this work, the question is in particular about why innovative growth companies are deciding to finance the public-sector and against private placement of the shares. -- The examination of the various possible motives of an exchange-market start is first based on theory, taking into account the specificities of the innovation process. Subsequently, the theoretical considerations in the context of a comprehensive study of the stock market newcomers in the New Market and in other German market segments are subjected to empirical review. -- The examination of the material financing theoretical work shows that the advantages of a stock market start ultimately correspond to the broad distribution of the share market, the information aggregation in the secondary market prices and the directness of the capital-allocation relationship. -- The results of the empirical investigation are particularly significant in the case of the two-participating companies.
content.title_en: Motives of the IPO on the New Market : Public financing of innovations from a theoretical and empirical perspective

content.text: The basic symmetry of the symmetry is performed with the same frequency of the symmetry. For this work, specific symmetry models are investigated. These models are from the field of theoretical solid-state physics, where they serve to describe the electron structure of strongly correlated solids. The molecular-specific parameters of the model are obtained directly from ab-initio calculations. To solve the electron-structure problem, the method of exact diagonalization has been implemented and parallelized. System-specifically, an electron-phonon coupling is introduced, symmetries are used and approximation methods developed. The approximations combine a local description of d-orbitals with a molecular orbital approach for s- and p-orbital, they provide in favorable cases a correlation energy with a fault of a few promille in comparison to the exact solution at a significantly reduced calculation time. With these methods, three problems have been investigated. First, the effect of strong electron correlation on the charge transfer in Creutz-taube-ktion has been analyzed with a local frequency of the symmetry.

content.text: Probabilistic life-cycle models for thermomechanical fatigue of soldering compounds in CSP components. Summary: The aim of this work was to create a reliability model for Chip Scale Package (CSP) which can be used to estimate the life of components under changed ambient loads, or newly developed components. One prerequisite for this is the determination of basic data for the representation of assembly reliability with components such as μBGA (Micro Ball Grid Array) and QFN (Quad Flat No Lead), as well as lead-free solders for thermal alternating loads. In the work, all relevant influencing variables that influence the life of the assemblies are to be found and converted into a universal reliability model for the various CSPs. The investigated designs include various μBGA and QFN. The focus of the investigations was on thermomechanical issues.
content.title_en: Probabilistic life models for thermomechanical fatigue of solder joints in CSP components

content.title_en: Media culture : Stories - Discourses - Designs

content.text: Ar@chitekturen in Zelluloid : The cinematic view of space. In the subject of architecture and film, the first thing you associate is scenery or set design, thinking of films like »Metropolis« or »Blade Runner«. This book proposes a new perspective: it shows the means by which the film designs spaces, awakens emotions and lets the viewer immerse themselves in an illusion space. This knowledge is also of great interest for the architectural spatial design. Thus, filmic spatial concepts such as editing or the cadration from the point of view of architecture are considered and discussed from the point of view of perception theory. Theoretical approaches and exemplary study examples create an intermedial interface that creates a new understanding of the origin of spatial effects.
content.title_en: Ar@chitectures in Celluloid : The cinematic view of the room

content.text: Optimization of the use of unmanned flight systems using mathematical optimization methods. In particular, the linearization of circles or balls by means of the method of Glineur can be successfully implemented and tested. It was shown that a trajectory under temporal and local boundary conditions could be solved plausibly with the given formulas. Furthermore, it was illustrated that such problems can also be solved with simple hardware and software. Only with increasing complexity and secondary conditions it leads the system to the limits.
content.title_en: Optimization of the use of unmanned flight systems using mathematical optimization methods

content.text: "Thank you for your entry into the logbook" : literary mass communication on the social web. Summary: This paper examines various variants of literary mass communication on the social web. After an introductory chapter, which also explains the technical framework conditions of online communication, the special features of mass communication on various social web platforms are illuminated. In the main part of the dissertation, the author presents various projects of literary mass communication, including literature on Twitter, sequel novels on Facebook, literature and secondary literary communication on literary platforms as well as literary communication on blogs and much more. In this context, the special production conditions are examined, the texts undergo an analysis and the distribution as well as the connection communication via social channels. In a final chapter the specific attraction of participation in literary online mass communication on the social web is elaborated. The work sees itself as a broad analysis of a field of literary communication that has so far been little considered.
content.title_en: "Thank you for your entry in the logbook" : literary mass communication in the social web

content.text: The purpose of Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) is to classify and manage information at a cost. Rapid data growth, high storage, administration and operating costs as well as numerous legal requirements are the main reasons for the emergence of ILM. To analyse the cost and benefit ratio that arises in the implementation and application of ILM, this work will simulate and evaluate a process for the economic analysis of the management of unstructured data in the ILM. It will examine the influence of automated classification and management on varying amounts of data with varying access frequencies and usage levels to the economy of the ILM, in addition to the management of the internal data analysis, the management of the cloud is also involved in the management of the business.

content.text: Deinstitutionalization of the humanities through organisational change: self-determination and participation of disabled people as a challenge for change processes in organizations. This work explores the extent to which the reforms of the housing-related services of the so-called disability assistance required in the field of healing education under the term deinstitutionalization can be realized by a change of the organizations addressed. The core of the work is an empirical study on the decentralisation and regionalization of a large and complex institution. The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the deinstitutionalisation of the medical educational discourse and is supplemented and further developed by an institution-sociological perspective of neo-institutionalism. The qualitative study subsequently analyses the structural and substantive facets of the change of the large and complex institution in its interaction. The results thus show the complexity of the change processes, especially in terms of the everyday reality of residents in stationary settings. The rebinding of the empirical results on the deinstitutionalization theory (heilopädagogik and neoinstitutionalism) is a key element of an active strategy of deinstitutionalizationalization. The DIP is a passively disabled of the participation in the production of the humanities.
content.title_en: Deinstitutionalisation through organisational change: self-determination and participation of disabled people as a challenge for change processes in organisations

content.text: The work deals with the legal classification of networks. For this purpose, the understanding of networks in sociology, economics, politics and geography is first analyzed. The work then deals with the recognition of network relationships in the legal system. The legal assessment begins with the question whether and to what extent relationships between network actors are subject to contract law. In this respect, the bipolar starting point for most legal standardisations is already a major challenge. Furthermore, the social, property, enrichment and criminal law is viewed. The latter areas of law are particularly important because network-oriented actions do not necessarily have to be linked to a contractual relationship. Finally, special forms of action are considered legally, which have a particularly high network orientation according to the economic science perspective.
content.title_en: Network relations in the civil law system

content.text: Collecting things, creating knowledge: The history of natural history collections in Basel, 1735-1850. content.text: Physical hydrogels on polyurethane basis. Physical hydrogels are currently becoming increasingly interested in the cell substrates, as viscoelasticity or stress relaxation is an important parameter in mechanotransduction, which has been neglected so far. In this work, multi-functional polyurethanes have been designed, which form physical hydrogels via a novel geling mechanism. In water, the anionic polyurethanes spontaneously form aggregates, which are held in solution by electrostatic rejection. A fast geling can be achieved from here by charge shielding, which leads to aggregation and a network is formed. This can be done by adding different acids or salts, so that both acidic (pH 4-5) and pH neutral hydrogels can be obtained. While conventional hydrogels on polyurethane basis are usually produced by toxic isocyanate-containing prepolymers, the physical geling mechanism described here is suitable for use in sensitive environments. While conventional hydrogels on polyurethane basis can be characterized by an excellent hydrogel generation independently of the over-relation.
content.title_en: Physical hydrogels based on polyurethane

content.text: Efficient and accurate evaluation of aggregation into totals in population balance equations. Applications of population balance equations can be found in many chemical production processes such as crystallization or production of pharmaceuticals. In such equations, an aggregation process is described by source and sink integrale. The numerical analysis of the source integral is usually of square order. In this dissertation, we focus on the efficient evaluation of such aggregation integrale and reduce the complexity to quasilinear. We provide numerous numerical tests for various initial values that provide (heuristic) strategies for the choice of the discretization parameters. Applications of population balance equations can be found in many chemical production processes, e.g. crystallization and precision of pharmaceutical materials. In population balance equations the aggregation process is determined by quantity and quantity in aggregate.
content.title_en: Efficient and accurate evaluation of aggregation integrals in population balance equations
